‘Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely’: Trump envoy warns Iran amid US standoff
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:44:24 UTC
02:44:24 KST

U.S. Ambassador to Turkey and President Donald Trump's special envoy Tom Barrack said Friday that an American strike on Iran was possible as early as this weekend. Asked by online commentator Mario Nawfal whether a strike could take place over the weekend, Barrack replied: "Absolutely." However, Barrack immediately stressed that Washington remained open to a diplomatic agreement with Tehran. "The president is very clear. He's open and available and accessible to a deal," Barrack said, adding that negotiations had been underway for months. 
Hours later, Trump also raised the possibility of another U.S. military operation if Tehran failed to reach an agreement. "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree," he said. "If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business.' But, you know, I doubt they'll do that because perhaps they're not smart."
His remarks contrasted with the White House's statement Thursday that the United States would not resume attacks on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly explicitly ruled out American strikes before the vote, although officials said Trump continued to keep military options available. 
Meanwhile, the Financial Times reported that Washington was preparing for a prolonged confrontation with Iran, citing an interview with Mike Waltz, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, as the administration seeks to use military and economic pressure to extract concessions from Tehran in stalled negotiations.
Waltz was asked whether the United States could still find itself in a deadlock with Iran a year from now, without an agreement on its nuclear program or a return to prewar shipping conditions in the Strait of Hormuz.
"I'm not going to put out hypotheticals," Waltz told the Financial Times, expressing hope that Iran would return to serious negotiations well before then.
However, he emphasized that "the president and the US Navy can maintain this blockade for the foreseeable future," referring to restrictions on Iranian ports. Waltz also said the administration was tightening its economic pressure campaign. 
Waltz subsequently challenged the Financial Times' characterization of his remarks as a warning that Washington was prepared for a prolonged confrontation. Responding to coverage of the interview, he said the newspaper had misrepresented his statements and emphasized that decisions on how long to maintain the blockade and pursue diplomacy rested with Trump. 
Meanwhile, Trump has repeatedly threatened to launch renewed strikes against Iran following the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, just one week after Israel's own elections.
Speaking to reporters outside the White House on Friday, Trump suggested that Washington could bring the war to a swift conclusion but was weighing whether to do so or allow the conflict to weaken gradually.
"We could end it very quickly," Trump said. "Do we want to finish it off or just want to let it wither?"
Trump also described Iran as a failing state and touted what he presented as American achievements in the conflict, including increased oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. He claimed the United States was obtaining the results it wanted. 
The war, which Trump initially said would last four to five weeks, is now approaching its ninth month. It has driven gasoline prices to record highs as Iran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important maritime trade routes.
Perhaps even more significantly for Trump, the war has severely damaged his popularity in the United States, including among Republican voters. His approval rating has fallen to approximately 31%, less than two weeks before the midterm elections.
The Republican Party also faces the possibility of losing control of both chambers of Congress, amid growing public frustration over high prices.
In an effort to bring down fuel costs, Trump reached an agreement this month with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Russian diesel to be sold to the United States after years of sanctions. The move drew sharp criticism from Western leaders, who warned that the revenues would provide Moscow with a financial lifeline to continue its war against Ukraine, which is approaching its fifth year.
Waltz, who according to the Financial Times had advocated U.S. support for Ukraine's government while serving in Congress in 2024, defended Trump's agreement.
He argued that the arrangement was necessary to address a global shortage of refined petroleum products that had affected industries ranging from aviation to agriculture. Waltz said fertilizer shortages were contributing to a humanitarian crisis in East Africa.
According to Waltz, Trump was balancing global energy needs, particularly the supply of diesel. He suggested that revenues from the arrangement could also encourage Russia to engage seriously in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Ukraine.
Plans for a brief, intense strike
Earlier this week, The New York Times reported that the U.S. and Israeli militaries had developed detailed plans to resume strikes against Iran following the American midterm elections early next month.
American officials and sources familiar with the discussions said preparations were progressing for a brief, intense operation, likely involving attacks on nuclear and energy facilities, as well as missile and drone systems.
Senior Iranian officials said they were aware of the American and Israeli war plans and were developing new targets and tactics of their own. Among other measures, Iranian officials have threatened to target data centers and undersea internet cables, warning that any renewed confrontation would not be brief.
Peyman Salehi, a political analyst in Tehran, said that if Iran were attacked, its response could include strikes on major oil refineries in Saudi Arabia, including facilities operated by the national oil company Aramco.
According to Salehi, such strikes would trigger an immediate and sharp rise in global oil and energy prices. He argued that the war had demonstrated that increasing energy costs was one of Tehran's most effective means of exerting pressure on Trump because of the economic consequences for American consumers.
The New York Times stressed that no American decision to launch an attack had yet been made.
An earlier Financial Times report said the IDF had prepared for several days of fighting with Iran about a week and a half ago, but Trump opposed resuming hostilities before the American midterm elections and blocked the move. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu subsequently denied that report.

US Justice Department seeks to block Alaska Senate election certification if Dan Sullivan loses
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:43:54 UTC
02:43:54 KST

Diyar Guldogan
23 October 2026•Update: 23 October 2026
 The Trump administration filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent Alaska from certifying its US Senate election results under certain circumstances involving the candidacy of a second candidate named Dan J. Sullivan, according to the lawsuit.
The complaint, filed on Thursday in the US District Court for the District of Alaska, names the state and several election authorities as defendants and seeks declaratory and injunctive relief statewide.
The legal action could have implications for the state’s closely watched Senate race, in which incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan is seeking reelection against Democrat Mary Peltola.
According to allegations in the lawsuit, Dan J. Sullivan entered the race “with the intention of misleading” supporters of the incumbent and creating voter confusion because of their similar names.
The filing argues that certifying results affected by the second candidate’s appearance on the ballot would undermine the state’s responsibility to protect election integrity.
“Should Alaska certify any electoral results tainted by the inclusion on the ballot of Daniel J. Sullivan … the State and its officers will fail in its obligation to protect the integrity of its election,” the complaint stated.
The Justice Department’s filing comes as both parties compete for control of the Senate in the November midterm elections. Alaska is generally considered a Republican-leaning state, and President Donald Trump won it by a double-digit margin in the 2024 presidential election.
‘The Daniel J. is the fake’
Asked about the Alaska election lawsuit, President Donald Trump said: “I'm the one that said 'do it'.”
“They have two guys run named Dan Sullivan. So the Democrats put up a guy ... I don't think he ever voted before. All of a sudden he decides to run for the Senate, and his name is Dan Sullivan. One is Daniel S., one is Daniel J..The Daniel J. is the fake,” Trump said.
He said Daniel J. has “nothing to do with politics. It's a disgrace.”
Later, addressing a rally in the state of Florida, Trump accused Democrats of trying to confuse voters in Alaska’s Senate race by fielding a candidate with the same name as incumbent Sen. Sullivan.
“We have a man named Dan Sullivan. So the Democrats, maybe here they're not so dumb. They put another man also with the name of Dan Sullivan. So we have two Dan Sullivans. How about that?” Trump told his supporters.
The president argued that the presence of two candidates with similar names could create confusion among voters ahead of the November midterm elections.
“That's not so dumb, actually. It's cheating like hell, but it's not the dumbest thing in the world, and it's very confusing to people, to put it mildly,” Trump said.

Meloni meets Kuwait Emir, open to extending Q8 fuel price cap
'Diplomatic engagement yields significant measures for citizens and businesses'
ROME,
23 October 2026, 19:42
ANSA English Desk
Share
Link copiato
- ALL RIGHTS RESERVED
During a bilateral meeting between
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and the Emir of Kuwait, the
Kuwaiti side expressed a willingness to extend the price cap on
gasoline and diesel—a measure already implemented by Q8 in
recent weeks in response to the government's appeal to curb
energy costs and protect families and businesses, ccording to
sources at Palazzo Chigi.
They said the Emir's willingness to do so serves as "a concrete
sign of the solid relationship between Italy and Kuwait, and of
the Italian government's ability to foster constructive dialogue
with strategic partners—translating diplomatic engagement into
significant measures for citizens and the productive sector."

Moldova declares Russian Embassy employee persona non grata after drone incident
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:42:58 UTC
02:42:58 KST

Kanyshai Butun
23 October 2026•Update: 23 October 2026
Moldova has declared a Russian Embassy employee persona non grata after a Russian drone crashed on its territory, President Maia Sandu said on Friday.
“We condemn this latest dangerous act,” Sandu said on the US social media platform X, stressing that the drone violated Moldovan airspace.
The Foreign Ministry also condemned the alleged airspace violation, after a drone carrying explosives landed about 100 meters from a residential home in the village of Chistelnita.
The incident constitutes a serious violation of Moldova’s sovereignty and security, and poses a direct threat to the safety of its citizens, the ministry said.
“Such actions are unacceptable and demonstrate, once again, the risks stemming from the Russian Federation’s war of aggression against Ukraine,” the ministry said, calling on Moscow to cease actions that "endanger regional security and human lives."
Russia has yet to comment on Moldova’s latest statement.

Zelenskyy says restrictions on Starlink remain in force
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
20:42:00 EEST
02:42:00 KST

Zelenskyy says restrictions on Starlink remain in force
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed that speed restrictions for Starlink satellite communications terminals in Ukraine remain in force.
Source: Zelenskyy during an online meeting at the Hudson Institute on 23 October, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine
Quote: "The speed limits on Starlink and Starshield are still there. The speed has not been restored. And the delivery of interceptors to protect us against Russian ballistic missiles is still delayed.
We are waiting for interceptors that were already agreed on but they are still not coming. Hope that everything is on the way. And this is a real problem for us because the Russians attack almost every day, Russia attacks us massively. So that's where things stand today."
Details: The president said that this is happening while Ukraine continues successful operations on the front line.
Zelenskyy added that he wants relations with America and all other partners to be as strong as possible.
Quote: "Without America, without a strong America and an America that cares about what happens in the world, the world would definitely be a worse place. These days people ask why Ukraine is speaking more openly directly to the world.
The answer is simple. We want people to understand us, and I mean people, societies, nations, as many people as possible. And when people understand what is really going on, political leaders can take a stronger path. The one that can really bring peace closer."
Background:
- The WSJ, citing US and Ukrainian officials familiar with the matter, reported that Trump had called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions on the military version of Starlink in Ukraine.
- On the evening of 22 October, Trump said that Elon Musk has lifted speed restrictions on the military version of Starlink in Ukraine but declined to say whether he had personally called Musk about the matter.
- The Ministry of Defence of Ukraine reported that it was continuing to record disruption to Starlink/Starshield services on the front line.

Bayern Munich coach Kompany hospitalized after collapsing during training
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:41:59 UTC
02:41:59 KST

Halis Sunnetci
23 October 2026•Update: 23 October 2026
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalized Friday after collapsing while watching a training session involving the German club’s reserve team, Bayern announced.
The 40-year-old Belgian coach required medical attention while observing the second team’s training session and will undergo thorough examinations at a hospital, the club said in a statement.
Kompany will remain under medical care, while his coaching staff will oversee training and matches until further notice.
“The health of Vincent Kompany is our highest priority,” Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said.
“We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to help him recover quickly. Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs,” he added.
Kompany had recently been suffering from a viral infection that forced him to miss training sessions and a news conference ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League match against Arsenal.
He returned to the touchline for the 2-2 draw and later acknowledged that he had ignored his body’s warning signs while battling the illness.
The cause of Friday’s collapse has not been disclosed, and Bayern has not provided a timetable for his return.
Bayern, who lead the Bundesliga standings, are scheduled to face Freiburg away on Sunday.

EU announces additional $25M in humanitarian aid for Yemen
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:41:09 UTC
02:41:09 KST

Necva Tastan Sevinc
23 October 2026•Update: 23 October 2026
The European Commission on Friday announced an additional €22.5 million ($25 million) in humanitarian assistance for Yemen as renewed fighting deepens needs and forces thousands from their homes.
The funding comes on top of €87.5 million previously allocated for 2026, bringing the total to €110 million.
“Yemen is once again caught in the violence of war, while its humanitarian crisis remains largely forgotten,” said Hadja Lahbib, the EU commissioner for preparedness and crisis management.
“Families cannot wait for a ceasefire to put food on the table or find a safe place to sleep. Civilians on all sides are paying a terrible price.”
Nearly 230,000 people have been displaced in recent weeks, the European Commission said, warning that military escalation has increased civilian casualties and disrupted essential services and humanitarian assistance.
“Attacks that kill civilians and destroy hospitals, homes and essential services must stop. All parties must respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians,” Lahbib said.
The additional funding will help aid partners respond to growing needs, strengthen operational capacity and pre-position critical supplies, prioritizing displaced families, women, children, people with disabilities and marginalized communities.
Some 22.3 million people in Yemen require humanitarian assistance and protection. Around 5.2 million are internally displaced, while more than 2.2 million children under five suffer from acute malnutrition, according to the EU.
“The people of Yemen must not be forgotten. The EU will stand by them for as long as it takes,” Lahbib said.

German ambassador: Ukraine is vital to Europe's defence, and its role in security revolves around NATO
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
20:41:00 EEST
02:41:00 KST

German ambassador: Ukraine is vital to Europe's defence, and its role in security revolves around NATO
Germany's ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge, has said that Ukraine is already contributing to the joint defence of Europe and expressed the conviction that the European security system with Ukrainian involvement will revolve around NATO.
Source: European Pravda, citing the ambassador's remarks in an interview
Details: Ruge noted that NATO leaders determined at the Washington summit that Ukraine's future is in the Alliance.
Quote: "So when this will happen – again, it's a political issue. The difference that we have today, at least from a German point of view, is: it's very clear that Ukraine is not just the recipient of our assistance. Ukraine is also a big element of the defence of Europe today. We need Ukraine, with its armed forces and its competence in modern warfare, to be part of our defence."
Details: Asked how he sees Europe's security structure and Ukraine's role in it, Ruge replied: "I think it revolves around NATO, in my mind."
Quote: "I'm a former NATO person, so maybe that's logical, but NATO is the organisation that is in charge of collective defence."
Details: Ruge acknowledged that the US's role in NATO is changing, particularly with regard to changes in the priorities for deploying American troops.
Quote: "So Europeans will have to step up, we'll have to play more of a role. But in my mind, Ukraine is already very, very close to NATO. We have the NATO-Ukraine Council. We do a lot of things together. We have the joint analysis, training and education centre in Bydgoszcz in Poland. We are learning from Ukraine today when it comes to unmanned systems."
Details: Ruge added that he does not know exactly when Ukraine will become a full member of NATO.
Quote: "But we want – from a German point of view – Ukraine to be as close to NATO as possible, because in reality you were already part of our collective defence."
Background:
- Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna has expressed the view that admitting Ukraine into NATO could stop the spiral of war that began in 2008 with Russia's attack on Georgia.
- Ukraine's Ambassador to NATO Aliona Hetmanchuk said in early July that Ukraine's goal of joining the Alliance remains unchanged, and that an increasing number of countries understand that having Ukraine as a member would be of greater benefit to NATO itself.

Five more children returned to Ukrainian-controlled territory
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:40:00 UTC
02:40:00 KST

Five more children returned to Ukrainian-controlled territory
According to Ukrinform, Kherson Region Governor Oleksandr Prokudin reported this on Facebook.
"Five more children have been brought back to Ukrainian-controlled territory from the temporarily occupied part of the Kherson region. They include two girls and three boys aged 15 to 17," Prokudin said.
According to Prokudin, one of the children rescued was a 16-year-old girl who had witnessed an armed search by Russian troops during which they took her father away.
"Under threat, she was forced to attend a Russian school, where she was involved in propaganda events, taught to disassemble weapons, and made to perform in front of Russian military personnel. The girl also lived in constant fear because of drone attacks on civilians," he added.
The children were returned with the assistance of the charitable organization Save Ukraine. They are now safe and receiving the necessary assistance.
Since the beginning of 2026, a total of 235 children have been returned to Ukrainian-controlled territory from the temporarily occupied part of the Kherson region.
"Efforts to bring our children home continue under Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's Bring Kids Back UA initiative," Prokudin added.
As Ukrinform reported, Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets said that 24,953 people, including 2,054 children, had returned to Ukraine through the Mokrany-Domanove checkpoint between May 24, 2024, and October 15, 2026. This year alone, 11,815 people, including 802 children, have returned.

Stefanchuk, Hungarian Parliament speaker discuss historical issues
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
20:39:28 EEST
02:39:28 KST

Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada Ruslan Stefanchuk, who is on a working visit to Hungary, met with Speaker of the Hungarian National Assembly (parliament) Ágnes Forszthoffer, according to a post on the Ukrainian parliament's Telegram channel on Friday.
"They discussed the shared tragic chapters in the history of the two countries, in particular the Soviet repressions and the forced deportations of Hungarians. Ruslan Stefanchuk recalled an important step taken by the Verkhovna Rada – the adoption of a resolution recognizing and condemning the crimes committed by the Soviet military administration against Hungarians in 1944-1946. He also presented the Hungarian National Museum with a signed copy of this resolution," the statement reads.
As previously reported, Stefanchuk began his visit by paying tribute to the memory of Hungarians who were forcibly deported to the USSR by the Soviet totalitarian regime. He announced a meeting with Hungarian partners and his participation in events marking the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution.

Another five children return from occupied Kherson region; total reaches 235 since start of year – administration
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
20:39:02 EEST
02:39:02 KST

Head of Kherson Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Prokudin said five more children had been returned to territory controlled by Ukraine from the temporarily occupied part of Kherson region: two girls and three boys aged 15 to 17.
"One of the rescued children is a 16-year-old girl who survived an armed raid by Russian soldiers, during which they took her father away. Under threat, she was forced to attend a Russian school, where she was involved in propaganda activities, taught how to disassemble weapons, and forced to perform in front of Russian soldiers," Prokudin said on Telegram on Friday.
According to him, the children are currently safe and receiving the necessary assistance.
"Since the beginning of 2026, 235 children have already been returned from the temporarily occupied Kherson region to territory controlled by Ukraine," the head of the regional administration said.
Prokudin said the children's return was facilitated by the charity Save Ukraine, and the effort to bring them home continues as part of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's "Bring Kids Back UA" initiative.
In late September, Head of the Bring Kids Back UA presidential initiative Maksym Maksymov told Interfax-Ukraine that 2,616 children had been returned to Ukraine under the initiative since the start of the full-scale invasion, of whom 673 returned this year. Prokudin reported at the time that 190 children had been returned since the beginning of the year from the temporarily occupied part of Kherson region alone.

Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany hospitalised after collapse during training

Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:37:45 UTC
02:37:45 KST

A few weeks ago, sporting director Max Eberl said that Kompany, who reportedly needed help climbing stairs, had been struggling with both a viral infection and a hip injury.
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital by ambulance on Friday after collapsing at the club's training ground.
He reportedly collapsed after observing a training session involving Bayern's reserve team at the Sabener Strasse facility in Munich.
"Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's amateurs," a statement from the Bundesliga club read.
Emergency services were called to the scene, with German newspaper Bild reporting that a rescue helicopter also landed at the training complex.
Last week, it was reported that Kompany was suffering from a viral infection affecting his legs, raising doubts over his availability for Wednesday's Champions League match against Arsenal.
However, he returned to the dugout for the match and had only resumed training duties a few days before Friday's incident.
A former captain of the Belgian national team, Kompany started his managerial career six years ago and has been with Bayern since May 2024.

In Russia, the &quot;Proton&quot; plant that manufactured components for killing Ukrainians was attacked — partisans revealed the details
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
20:37:41 EEST
02:37:41 KST

In Russia, the "Proton" plant that manufactured components for killing Ukrainians was attacked — partisans revealed the details
Kyiv • UNN
At least four explosions were heard near the "Proton" plant in Oryol, Russia. "ATESH" reported the destruction of dozens of the enterprise's employees .
In the Russian city of Oryol, the Proton plant came under attack; components manufactured there are used in Iskander-M missiles and Pantsir-S1 systems, UNN reports, citing Astra.
Details
According to Astra, JSC Proton is a plant that manufactures semiconductor devices, LEDs, and electronic components for industry and special-purpose equipment. According to the Ukrainian side, its components are used in Russian weapons, including Iskander-M missiles and Pantsir-S1 systems.
Local residents reported at least four explosions. A large column of smoke rose over the city. Before that, a missile alert had been declared in the region. There is currently no official information about the consequences of the strike or any casualties.
In addition
Later, the ATESH partisan movement reported that dozens of valuable Proton plant employees had been killed in the Russian city of Oryol.
ATESH agents report that the missile strike was carried out precisely during the workers' shift change.
As a result, several dozen employees who produced components for killing Ukrainians were eliminated. We continue to collect information
The partisans confirmed that the Proton enterprise manufactures optoelectronic equipment and electronic components for Russia's military-industrial complex. Its products are used in Iskander-M missiles, Pantsir-S1 systems, and other military equipment.

Cyprus police investigate Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich for possible tax evasion after reports implicate accounting giant Deloitte
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:36:51 UTC
02:36:51 KST

Cyprus police investigate Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich for possible tax evasion after reports implicate accounting giant Deloitte
Police in Cyprus have launched an investigation into reports that Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich may have evaded taxes with help from the accounting firm Deloitte. A Cypriot Justice Ministry official told a parliamentary committee meeting on combating money laundering that the investigation was underway, the BBC reported.
The police financial crime unit is conducting the investigation.
“We will look at any company or person who may be involved. We will see if there has been fraud or if some documents have been manipulated,” Cypriot police spokesman Andreas Anastasiades told the BBC.
The BBC, The Guardian, and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ) previously published investigations reporting that Deloitte, one of the world’s largest consulting and accounting firms, helped falsify documents to conceal Abramovich’s wealth and help him evade taxes. According to the journalists, Deloitte’s Cyprus division helped him conceal $672 million in assets, including mansions, yachts, and private jets.
Abramovich’s lawyers denied any wrongdoing. Deloitte Cyprus said it had always complied with local laws.

Soccer team leaves pitch following racist insult but handed 0-3 forfeit loss
Italy
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
19:36:35 CEST
02:36:35 KST

After a teammate was subjected to
racist insults, the players of an Italian lower-tier soccer team
walked off the pitch but their act of solidarity and protest
resulted in a forfeit loss of 0-3 instead of them being rewarded
for their gesture.
                                    
Mascarino, a team competing in the Terza Categoria tier in the
province of Bologna, which faced Vigor Pieve 1925 on Sunday, is
now preparing an appeal.
                                    
The incident occurred in the 41st minute of the second half,
with the score at 0-1. The player responsible for the
discriminatory remarks was immediately sent off, but Mascarino
chose to abandon the match.
                                    
Vigor Pieve filed a complaint, and the sports judge, Carlo Del
Percio, handed down a 10-match suspension to the individual who
made the insult, while also awarding a 0-3 forfeit victory to
Vigor Pieve.
                                    
When contacted, the Bologna branch of the Italian Football
Federation (FIGC) declined to comment.
                                    
The penalized club is currently preparing an appeal, focusing on
Article 10 of the Code of Sports Justice—the provision cited in
the ruling—which states in its first paragraph: "A club held
responsible for events or circumstances that have affected the
orderly conduct of a match, or that have prevented the match
from taking place as scheduled, shall be penalized with the loss
of the match, recorded as a 0-3 forfeit defeat."
However, paragraph five—which will be the focal point of the
appeal—states: "When events occur during a match that, by their
very nature, cannot be assessed using purely technical criteria,
the sports justice bodies shall determine whether, and to what
extent, such events influenced the proper conduct of the match."
In such cases, the measures that may be taken include awarding a
forfeit loss or ordering a replay of the match deemed to have
been irregular.
                                    
The latter is the outcome requested by Mascarino.
                                    
Following the uproar caused by their formal complaint and the
subsequent victory awarded by default, Vigor Pieve's president
had indicated that the club might consider a request to replay
the match; however, they will not be able to do so.
                                    
The decision will rest with the fifth-tier sports justice body,
assuming—as is now certain—that Mascarino files an appeal
against the sports judge's ruling, in the belief that a
different assessment could be reached.
                                    
"We will evaluate whether to pursue criminal action against the
player who made the racist insult, and for our next match, we
will show up with only seven players; one of them will
immediately leave the pitch, triggering a suspension, a forfeit
loss, and a points deduction," Mascarino president Antonello Le
Fosse told Il Resto del Carlino newspaper.

Ethiopia's Tigray rebels urged to disarm
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:36:28 UTC
02:36:28 KST

Breadcrumb
Ethiopia's Tigray rebels urged to disarm as commander vows to fight on
An official in Tigray’s new federal-backed administration urged rebel fighters to lay down their weapons Friday, hours after a rebel commander called for continued resistance despite losing the northern Ethiopian region’s capital.
The calls to surrender and fight on came nearly three weeks after rebels lost control of Mekelle. At a hospital in the city, two wounded men said a drone strike killed four civilians as they loaded goats onto a truck earlier this week.
Redae Halefom Woldeselassie, the caretaker administration’s chief executive for political and public mobilisation, said rebel forces were collapsing and urged fighters to enter a disarmament and reintegration program.
“This is not the time for settling scores, I call upon you to return to your homes and continue your civilian lives,” he said in Mekelle.
He dismissed the prospect of the rebels retaking the city and portrayed the conflict as serving a small group of leaders rather than the people of Tigray.
Hours earlier, Lt. Gen. Fisseha Kidanu, identified in a television broadcast as commander of the Tigray army, pledged to reverse recent military setbacks.
“Local militias across the region — alongside all volunteers joining the resistance — are expected to engage the enemy,” he said Thursday night on Tigray Broadcast Media, a new rebel television station. His location was not disclosed.
Fisseha urged attacks on government-held positions despite his opponents’ advantages in drones and heavy weapons. The Tigray People’s Liberation Front, or TPLF, has also claimed to have inflicted heavy losses on government forces. The Associated Press could not independently verify those claims.
Government-allied fighters entered Mekelle on Oct. 4 after the TPLF withdrew. Ethiopia’s government subsequently established a six-month caretaker administration promising to restore services, help displaced people return and prepare for elections.
The government’s allies include the Tigray Peace Force, comprising former members of the TPLF’s armed wing — a division within Tigrayan forces that has complicated the renewed conflict.
Redae said Ethiopian troops and allied forces were conducting joint security operations, including measures to prevent looting. He promised preparations for displaced residents to return but gave no timetable.
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, speaking Monday to the Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation, accused the TPLF of acquiring weapons and forcibly recruiting young people instead of disarming under the November 2022 Pretoria peace agreement. He said his government had done everything within its capacity to implement the accord.
Wounded men describe drone strike 
At Ayder Hospital in Mekelle, Luel Berhanu, 22, and Samuel Belay, 20, said they were loading goats onto a truck in Finariwa, about 80 kilometers (49 miles) south of the city, when a strike hit around 9:30 p.m. Tuesday.
They said four civilians were killed and about six people wounded. The AP could not independently verify the casualties or establish who carried out the attack.
Luel said the truck’s headlights were on and a drone was hovering overhead shortly before the explosion. He said the blast severely injured his right eye and right arm, leaving him unable to see through that eye.
Samuel said they were working as day laborers loading the animals.
Hospital footage showed Luel with a bloodstained bandage covering his right eye and dressings around his shoulder and arm. Samuel lay on his side with an intravenous line attached to his arm.
A witness interviewed by the AP reported movements earlier that day by fighters identified as Agew Shengo, a militia that has previously fought alongside Tigrayan forces in neighboring Amhara region. Luel said rebel forces had been in the area several hours before the strike but none were present when it occurred.
Losing Mekelle may not end the war 
The renewed fighting has effectively shattered the Pretoria agreement, which ended the devastating 2020-2022 war.
Magnus Taylor, deputy Horn of Africa director at the International Crisis Group, told the AP last week that controlling towns and roads would not necessarily secure rural areas where Tigrayan fighters regrouped during the previous war.
“We shouldn’t imagine that this conflict is completely over just because the TPLF has lost Mekelle,” he said.

Chinese medical team holds free TCM outreach in Sierra Leone
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-24
01:35:45 CST
02:35:45 KST

FREETOWN, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 27th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone, in collaboration with local medical staff, on Thursday provided free Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) consultations, health education and practical training at the Calaba Town Health Center in the capital, Freetown, to mark the World Traditional Medicine Day.
The outreach, organized by the Traditional Chinese Medicine Center of the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital under China's "100 Medical Teams in 1,000 Villages" program, targeted patients suffering from neck, shoulder, lower back and limb pain.
The medical team applied techniques such as Fu's Subcutaneous Needling, balance-regulating acupuncture, Dong's extraordinary points, "tuina" massage and scraping therapy. Nearly 100 residents received treatment during the morning, with many reporting relief from chronic pain.
The team also conducted health education and hands-on training for local grassroots physicians in posture assessment, joint function evaluation, needling techniques and acupoint selection, using real clinical cases.
Mohamed K. Fabba, head of the Calaba Town Health Center, praised the initiative for addressing residents' healthcare needs and expressed hope for more outreach activities.
The medical team said it would expand grassroots services and technical training to promote traditional medicine cooperation between China and Sierra Leone under the China-Africa Health Partnership Initiative. ■

China Focus: Rescue efforts intensify after Xizang quake kills 16, injures 76
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-24
01:35:42 CST
02:35:42 KST

BAQEN, Xizang, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- Sixteen people have been killed and 76 others are injured following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Baqen County of the city of Nagqu in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region at 10:33 p.m. on Thursday, local authorities said.
The quake has also damaged or destroyed 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, according to a press conference held on Friday afternoon by the information office of the Nagqu municipal government.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, urging every effort to minimize casualties.
Xi also called for close monitoring of seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters, as well as proper accommodation for affected residents and swift repairs to damaged infrastructure.
Premier Li Qiang called for solid disaster prevention and response efforts, while the Ministry of Emergency Management (MEM) and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations.
China has allocated 50 million yuan (about 7.5 million U.S. dollars) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III.
More than 5,000 personnel have been deployed to the front lines of the disaster relief operation, working in teams responsible for search and rescue, medical treatment, temporary shelter and the provision of essential supplies.
An emergency command headquarters has been established on the front lines to coordinate relief efforts. As of 10 a.m. Friday, 12,489 residents have been evacuated.
After three rounds of comprehensive door-to-door checks, no missing persons had been reported as of 6 p.m. Friday, according to the emergency command headquarters.
In a village of Maru Township, one of the hardest-hit areas near the epicenter, Xinhua reporters saw many houses completely collapsed, while others sustained extensive wall damage. Rows of emergency tents were erected in an open, safe area below the village.
Half of villager Trinley's house collapsed, burying many of his belongings beneath the rubble. Two white tents were set up in his courtyard.
"After the earthquake, our biggest concerns were where to stay and what to eat," Trinley said. "The government provided us with supplies including emergency tents, water and instant noodles," he added.
The MEM said that on top of the 5,000 relief items previously allocated by the central government, an additional 5,000 central relief items, including tents, coats and folding beds were allocated.
By coordinating efforts with other relief agencies and companies, the ministry said that it has also promptly allocated 43,000 other relief items, including mobile toilets, heating stoves, food and fuel, to ensure that affected people are properly resettled.
The Red Cross Society of China has dispatched a working team to the disaster-hit area to guide local relief efforts. It has also allocated 3,800 sets of supplies, including family relief kits, hygiene kits, heaters, tents, jackets, folding beds and quilts. The society has additionally allocated 50 emergency toilet units to support affected residents and coordinated with the Chinese Red Cross Foundation to provide 500 family relief kits, 500 hygiene kits and more than 1,000 cartons of food to the quake-hit area. The China Charity Federation, one of the country's most influential charity organizations, has urgently allocated 3 million yuan to support emergency rescue endeavors.
RESCUE CHALLENGES
The earthquake zone has an average elevation of nearly 4,800 meters. The high-altitude, cold and low-oxygen environment, secondary disaster hazards and aftershock risks pose challenges to the relief efforts, local authorities said at the press conference.
Deng Xiaogang, a rescuer with Nagqu's fire and rescue team, said that beyond the low temperatures and low oxygen levels, the biggest challenge was that the epicenter was in a pastoral area, where residents live far apart, making search-and-rescue operations more time-consuming in the initial stages.
Some herding sites are up in the mountains, and the terrain is rugged, said Jigme Dorje, deputy head of the Baqen County public security bureau. "At first, machines could not reach these places, so we had to climb up and dig through the rubble with our hands, wearing only gloves," he said.
Local authorities said that rescue teams will continue to take precautions to overcome difficulties in relief operations.
Nighttime temperatures in the quake zone are low. Earthquake-triggered hazards such as landslides, collapses and falling rocks are currently the main secondary disaster risks.
Earthquake monitoring, meteorological and emergency management departments, meanwhile, are coordinating closely to issue timely warnings of aftershocks and adverse weather conditions.
Local authorities have launched round-the-clock intensified monitoring of key sites, including mountainsides, reservoirs, power stations, rivers, structurally unsafe buildings and telecommunications base stations. Emergency repairs are also underway, with damaged telecommunications and power facilities gradually being restored.
Pan Zhiqing, Party secretary of Nagqu's emergency management bureau, said that in follow-up rescue work, personnel will be assigned to accompany rescue teams to inspect geological hazards along mountains and roads. Dangerous areas will be immediately cordoned off, and people and vehicles will be prohibited from passing.
Transportation authorities will monitor road damage in real time, promptly repair and reopen blocked sections, and ensure smooth traffic flow. They will continue to coordinate with meteorological and natural resources departments and issue risk warnings, Pan added.
China Telecom, China Mobile and China Unicom mobilized emergency repair teams, vehicles and equipment overnight, dispatching personnel to the quake-hit areas to restore communications services and inspect network facilities.
All telecommunications base stations disrupted by the earthquake in Baqen County had been restored as of 10:30 a.m. Friday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration.
The 7.0-magnitude earthquake was an extensional rupture, according to experts with the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC).
"An extensional fracture, in simple terms, occurs when the crust is stretched horizontally and, under tension and gravity, faultage slides downward along existing faultage, forming fractures and rupture surfaces," said Han Yanyan, a senior engineer with the earthquake prediction department of the CENC. ■

China's top diplomat says Global Governance Initiative increasingly relevant
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-24
01:35:30 CST
02:35:30 KST

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, reads out a message from Chinese President Xi Jinping and delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) in Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province, Oct. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Mu Yu)
XIONGAN, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Friday that the Global Governance Initiative has become increasingly relevant one year after it was put forward, calling for efforts to turn its vision into reality.
Chinese President Xi Jinping put forward the Global Governance Initiative, offering a solution to address the governance deficit and jointly create a better future, Wang said in a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said countries should jointly uphold the central role of the United Nations, enhance the Security Council's rapid response capacity, and respond to the legitimate concerns of developing countries.
He said major countries must set an example in upholding equality, credibility, moral principles and cooperation, which is the only way to bring about a world where all countries coexist in harmony and all nations thrive in mutual appreciation.
All parties should adhere to a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security and resolve differences and disputes between countries through peaceful means to safeguard peace, he said.
It is important to enhance the representation and voice of the Global South in international affairs, advance reform of the international financial system in accordance with the timetable and roadmap agreed by all parties, increase the representation of developing countries in the Security Council, and give full play to the important role of emerging multilateral cooperation mechanisms such as BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, Wang said.
All countries should uphold the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core, keep development at the center of the international agenda, and fully implement the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, he said.
He also called for improving governance rules in emerging fields, turning new frontiers such as the deep sea, the polar regions and outer space into areas for international cooperation, and evolving an AI governance structure based on general consensus soon.
Hosted by the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs, the forum is themed "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World."
Nearly 400 representatives from strategic, political, academic, business, media, and youth sectors from more than 90 countries and international and regional organizations, including the UN, attended the opening ceremony. ■

China Focus: South China free-trade island builds space hub as new growth engine
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-24
01:35:27 CST
02:35:27 KST

HAIKOU, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- With giant lightning rods towering above the coastline of eastern Wenchang in south China, coconut groves have given way to rows of launch pads while the country's first commercial spaceport is coming to life.
Known as the Hainan commercial spacecraft launch site, the spaceport has become a cornerstone of China's endeavors to help Hainan make its emerging commercial space business a strategic growth engine across the island-wide free trade port.
"Launch orders are fully booked for this year and next. The earliest available slot is in the year after," said Zhang Xiaojun, deputy general manager of a Wenchang aerospace launch support company.
The facility's first phase, comprising launch pads 1 and 2, is already operational. Pad 2, equipped with a mobile launch platform and horizontal testing system, can accommodate more than 20 types of domestic rockets and complete preparations for a full launch cycle in as little as 66 hours.
Construction is in full swing on pads 3 and 4, which are expected to be ready by year-end. Once all four pads are online, the site will be capable of supporting approximately 60 launches per year.
But ambition stretches well beyond the launch pads.
Wenchang, the once unknown coastal fishing town, is rushing to build out a vertically integrated ecosystem, ranging from rocket and satellite manufacturing to downstream data services, under a model which officials describe as "Made in Wenchang, Launched from Wenchang."
A rocket assembly, testing and reuse facility, with its first phase having been established in Wenchang by a commercial space company, is operational. A string of other rocket-chain projects have also broken ground.
Additionally, a massive satellite manufacturing base has completed its production line and entered trial production in the city, with the first satellite expected to roll off the line by the end of 2026.
On the data side, progress has also been encouraging. An aerospace supercomputing center, which began operations in 2023, is helping Wenchang stitch together a full aerospace big-data value chain, from data acquisition and reception to storage, processing and commercial application.
Ye Shiyang, chairman of the center's operating company, said the firm has consolidated resources from 161 satellites in orbit to build a sub-meter-resolution commercial remote-sensing database. Leveraging the supercomputing center's processing power and Hainan Free Trade Port's cross-border data-flow policies, the company is expanding its "two ends abroad" data-processing model.
"Overseas clients send us satellite remote-sensing data for processing, and we deliver the finished products back to them," Ye said. In May, the company completed its first remote-sensing data export to Singapore and is in discussions with clients in Thailand, Cambodia and several European countries.
This convergence of rocket, satellite and data chains has drawn more than 700 companies into the satellite and rocket industrial park in Wenchang, creating what officials call a "front shop, back factory" ecosystem: satellites rolled off the production line can reach the launch pad just kilometers away.
At the national level, China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for accelerating the development of strategic emerging industries, including aerospace, and the China National Space Administration unveiled a special action plan in late 2025 to promote the high-quality, safe development of commercial space.
Hainan has moved quickly to align with this push, designating the sector as one of four industrial clusters each targeted to reach 50 billion yuan (about 7.4 billion U.S. dollars) in annual revenue, and positioning it as a key pillar in cultivating new quality productive forces.
"The layout in Wenchang is not just about rocket launches," said Zheng Ni, a division director at the Hainan Provincial Department of Science and Technology.
"The goal is to use the launch site to drive industrial development, building a full-chain cluster and developing rocket, satellite and data chains within an 'aerospace-plus' ecosystem to fuel Hainan's space-powered growth," Zheng said. ■

Explainer: Will new Russia-Ukraine talks deliver peace?
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-24
01:35:19 CST
02:35:19 KST

MOSCOW, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- Trilateral talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine are planned to be held in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, in the first half of November, with a focus on security issues after a peace settlement, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday.
Earlier on Wednesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reiterated his willingness to "freeze" the fighting along current battle lines as a "real way to end this war."
U.S. President Donald Trump said Moscow and Kiev are "maybe now the closest" they have been to reaching a settlement to the war.
Will renewed talks deliver a real peace?
PUSH FOR TALKS
Since the Russia-Ukraine conflict broke out in February 2022, more than four years have passed, punctuated by a succession of talks for a solution.
In a new diplomatic urge prior to the U.S. midterm election, U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff met Zelensky in Oslo on Tuesday before travelling to St. Petersburg to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin the following day. The discussions covered security guarantees for Ukraine, postwar reconstruction and the prospect of resuming trilateral talks involving Kiev, Moscow and Washington.
Putin agreed "in principle" to restart the negotiations after Nov. 10, focusing on establishing a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends, according to Kremlin foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov.
Zelensky said he was willing to consider freezing the conflict along the current front lines as a way to reach a peace deal with Russia and bring the years-long conflict to an end through diplomacy.
"We call it a ceasefire ... President Trump called it freeze and stop," Zelensky said, when asked whether he would agree to halt the fighting along the current front lines while retaining control of "75 percent or more" of the pre-war Ukrainian territory.
Washington is making little secret of its impatience to secure a Ukraine deal. Trump on Tuesday urged Zelensky to make a deal with Russia to end the conflict.
"We want Zelensky to make a deal," Trump told reporters at the White House. "If they don't make a deal, it's just gonna get worse."
"We have given tremendous amounts to Ukraine; we've got nothing back. Other than high diesel," Trump said. "The American taxpayers are tired of it."
"It's time to make a deal," he added, "Russia would like to get it done."
DIVERGING AGENDAS
Washington's rush for pressuring Zelensky to accept a fast deal is clearly seen. Trump stated publicly on Monday that Zelensky "doesn't want to stop" the conflict and "is not helping matters much. I think it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reportedly delayed the transfer of Patriot interceptor missiles from European allies to Ukraine, potentially weakening Ukraine's air defense capacity.
Meanwhile, Ukraine's access to Starshield was significantly curtailed in mid-October, disrupting drone operations and battlefield communications. Reuters reported that the order came from inside the White House, though Trump denied involvement.
U.S.-Ukraine relations have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel supply deal with Russia on Oct. 9, part of his efforts to lower fuel prices ahead of early November's midterm elections. With high fuel prices fueling domestic frustration over the cost of living, Washington's urgency to secure a ceasefire may also reflect mounting pressure on Republicans ahead of the vote.
Russia could use the current opportunity to improve ties with Washington without making major concessions on Ukraine, according to the Washington Post.
Putin said talks should focus on security guarantees for both Russia and Ukraine, and a broader European security framework. He reiterated that Russia wanted a lasting settlement rather than a temporary ceasefire.
Territorial disputes remain a major obstacle, as Moscow demands that Ukraine cede the entire Donbas region. For Russia, resuming talks offers a chance to expand its strategic room for maneuver.
Meanwhile, Ukraine is seeking a ceasefire and robust security guarantees to prevent further attack. Following talks with Witkoff in Oslo, Zelensky said his proposals included NATO Article 5-style guarantees, while stressing that territorial issues must be discussed at the highest level.
Ukraine's bid for resuming trilateral talks and its openness to a peace deal based on freezing the current front lines could help ease tensions with Washington and signal Kiev's willingness to resolve the conflict through negotiations.
DEEP DIVISIONS REMAIN
Although Russia, the United States and Ukraine may resume talks, a ceasefire agreement between Moscow and Kiev remains far from certain.
"As experience shows, the mere fact that negotiations are taking place does not mean that a peace agreement is likely to be reached anytime soon," Ukrainian political scientist Volodymyr Fesenko said.
Witkoff reportedly presented Putin an updated peace proposal developed in coordination with Ukraine and European partners following talks in Oslo. However, Ushakov said the proposals contained little "substance." Moscow agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks, but its lukewarm response underscored the lack of consensus on how to end the war.
Currently, Russia and Ukraine remain deeply divided over two key issues -- territory and security guarantees.
Territorial disputes remain a major sticking point. Zelensky signaled in a media interview on Thursday that Kiev would not accept Russia's demand for Ukraine's withdrawal from Donbas, while Moscow continues to insist that the entire region should come under Russian control. Recent statements suggest neither side has significantly changed its position.
The two sides also remain at odds over security guarantees. Ukraine seeks security assurances from the United States and Europe as part of a ceasefire deal, while Russia firmly opposes the deployment of Western military personnel and facilities in Ukraine.
Chen Yu, deputy director of the Institute of Eurasian Studies at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, said the conflict's core issues remain unresolved, with little room for compromise and the battlefield still deadlocked, making a political settlement unlikely in the near term.
Michael Kimmage, a foreign policy expert at the Brookings Institution think tank, told U.S. media that the Trump administration's "theory of the case is that by distancing themselves from Ukraine and by flattering the Russians, they can accomplish something at the bargaining table."
He is not, however, optimistic that the gambit will succeed.
"In the absence of a clear agenda coming from the White House and in the absence of very serious forms of leverage over Russia -- which the Trump administration has shied away from -- progress at the negotiating table is very difficult to imagine," he said. ■

Are Israel's drones signalling a new escalation with Hezbollah?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:34:45 UTC
02:34:45 KST

Breadcrumb
Are Israel's drones over Beirut signalling a coming escalation with Hezbollah?
Reports of increased Israeli drone activity over Beirut and its southern suburbs have raised questions about whether Israel is preparing for a new escalation against Hezbollah.
But while the flights have become more conspicuous in recent days, analysts told The New Arab that their presence alone does not establish that a wider offensive is imminent.
A report by local Lebanese news outlet Lebanon Files said Israeli reconnaissance flights had "returned" to Beirut and Mount Lebanon’s airspace. However, there is no publicly available evidence establishing that the flights had stopped before recently becoming more noticeable.
Israeli drones have continued to be reported over Beirut and its southern suburbs in recent months, including in reports published in September and footage circulated this week.
The question, therefore, is not simply whether the drones are present, but whether there has been a meaningful change in the frequency, duration or scope of their operations.
Surveillance and pressure on Hezbollah
Elijah J. Magnier, a veteran war correspondent and political analyst, told The New Arab that the activity should be taken seriously, while cautioning against treating visible drone flights as evidence of an imminent attack.
"Local reporting today documented a drone flying at low altitude over the southern suburbs. That establishes a visible presence; it does not, by itself, establish a sustained increase in surveillance or an imminent offensive," he said in comments to The New Arab on 21 October.
Magnier said Israeli drone flights could serve several purposes at once, including gathering intelligence, updating potential targets, monitoring movements and exerting psychological pressure on residents. A conspicuous presence over the capital can also serve as a reminder of Israel’s ability to strike south of Beirut.
If Israel were preparing another operation, surveillance could help it locate commanders, monitor weapons movements and identify suspected military infrastructure. But Magnier stressed that these remained possible objectives rather than evidence of a decision to launch an attack.
"Nor does identifying a target establish that a political decision to strike has been taken," he said. Without comparative flight data or intelligence about operational orders, he added, it was difficult to distinguish routine surveillance from preparations for a particular attack.
Nasser Khdour, an analyst at the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED), also said Israeli drone activity over Beirut was not new.
"Israel has continued gathering intelligence and identifying possible targets in preparation for another round of fighting," he told The New Arab.
Khdour suggested the more conspicuous drone presence was likely intended to increase pressure on Hezbollah and the Lebanese government during negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, with the Iran-backed militant group’s disarmament remaining a central point of disagreement.
The latest round of US-mediated military talks between Lebanese and Israeli delegations began in Tampa, Florida, on 20 October. The talks came amid continued Israeli attacks and demolitions in southern Lebanon, as well as renewed threats by Israeli officials against Hezbollah.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has warned Hezbollah against joining Iran in an attack on Israel, threatening a "powerful response" against Beirut’s southern suburbs, which would include a forced evacuation of the whole area. He has also threatened to expand the invasion towards Nabatieh and the Litani River in the south.
Hezbollah has refused to disarm as long as Israeli forces remain in Lebanon.
Could tensions with Iran draw Hezbollah into a wider war?
The risk of escalation also extends beyond Lebanon. With Israel’s general election scheduled for 27 October, renewed threats involving Iran have added another layer of uncertainty to the regional picture.
Magnier said electoral considerations were relevant to the analysis, but cautioned against presenting speculation about a war being launched for political reasons as an established plan. He said there was no publicly established evidence that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu intended to initiate a war to disrupt an election he expected to lose.
A renewed confrontation between Israel and Iran could, however, create a separate decision point for Hezbollah. Magnier said the group’s involvement would become a more serious possibility in such a scenario, but would remain a choice rather than an automatic consequence.
He also cautioned against assuming that Hezbollah’s weakened deterrence meant it had no remaining military capabilities. The group could seek to preserve its personnel and organisational structure while continuing to impose costs on Israel over time, rather than responding to every attack with a major escalation.
That calculation could change, he added, if civilian casualties mounted, senior leaders were targeted or Israel expanded its ground operations.
The conflict between Hezbollah and Israel began in October 2023 and was dramatically escalated by Israel into a full-scale war in September 2024. Fighting resumed on 2 March this year, alongside the US-Israeli war on Iran. Much of Hezbollah’s senior command structure has been eliminated over the past three years, and thousands of its fighters are believed to have been killed.
The drone flights therefore need to be viewed alongside the wider military and political context, rather than in isolation. Israel’s continued strikes, its threats against Beirut’s southern suburbs and the unresolved dispute over Hezbollah’s weapons all contribute to an already volatile situation.
For Magnier, the distinction remains between sustained pressure and a decision to launch a broader campaign. The visible presence of drones demonstrates Israel’s ability to monitor and threaten Hezbollah and its stronghold in Beirut's southern suburbs, but it does not reveal what Israeli leaders intend to do next.
"The drone flights show exposure and pressure. They do not yet tell us whether the next step will be surveillance, a targeted strike or a wider campaign," he said.

Finland May Have Quietly Handed Ukraine Its Rare ItO 90M Air Defense Fleet
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:30:33 UTC
02:30:33 KST

- Category
- World
Finland May Have Quietly Handed Ukraine Its Rare ItO 90M Air Defense Fleet
A previously undisclosed Finnish air-defense system has appeared in Ukrainian service, revealing that Helsinki quietly transferred rare ItO 90M launchers. These are now being used to defend the country from cruise missiles, aircraft, and Russia’s increasingly fast jet-powered drones.
Ukraine has now publicly confirmed the presence of Finland’s rare ItO 90M systems, showing that the launchers had been transferred without prior announcement and are already integrated into the country’s air-defense network against cruise missiles, aircraft, and jet-powered drones.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The Finnish ItO 90M short-range surface-to-air missile system appeared for the first time in footage released by Ukraine’s 1039th Anti-Aircraft Missile Regiment, according to Defense Express on October 23.
Until now, there had been no public indication that Ukraine had received the system. Finland never announced a transfer, and it remains unclear when the launchers arrived or how many were supplied.
The footage nevertheless indicates that the systems are already operational and being used in Ukraine’s air-defense network.
Finland’s Crotale on wheels
The ItO 90M is essentially Finland’s version of the French Crotale NG air-defense system, mounted on the Sisu XA-181 armored personnel carrier chassis.
Ukraine has already operated French Crotale NG systems since 2022, but the French military uses them primarily in a towed configuration. Finland’s version gives the system significantly greater mobility by integrating it onto an armored vehicle.
Both versions fire the VT-1 interceptor missile.
The missile can engage targets at ranges of up to 15 kilometers and altitudes of around 9 kilometers. It can accelerate to approximately 1,250 meters per second—about Mach 3.6, or roughly 2,800 mph—and carries a 13-kilogram warhead.
Those characteristics make the system suitable for engaging aircraft and helicopters, but Defense Express notes that its capabilities are particularly relevant for Ukraine because it can also intercept cruise missiles and high-speed UAVs, including Russia’s newer jet-powered drones.
Secret transfer of a rare system
The biggest unanswered question is how many ItO 90Ms Finland may have supplied.
Finland acquired just one prototype and 20 production systems during the 1990s, meaning its entire original inventory amounted to only 21 launchers.
Even if all the systems survived and remained serviceable, the fleet was tiny from the outset.
Defense Express therefore raises the possibility that Finland may have chosen to transfer a significant portion—or potentially even its entire remaining ItO 90M inventory—to Ukraine rather than retain a handful of systems requiring their own maintenance, training, and logistical support.
There is currently no confirmation that all 21 were transferred, however, and neither Helsinki nor Kyiv has disclosed the number delivered.
Already defending Ukrainian skies
Whatever the size of the transfer, the first public footage confirms that at least some Finnish ItO 90Ms are no longer sitting in storage or training units—they are already being used by Ukrainian air-defense troops.
Their appearance comes as Ukraine faces a rapidly evolving Russian aerial threat, including faster jet-powered drones that place greater demands on short-range air defenses.
With VT-1 missiles capable of speeds well above Mach 3, the Finnish systems provide another layer between Ukraine’s cheaper interceptor drones and its more expensive long-range air-defense systems.
Previously, reports emerged that Finland is already preparing its 36th military aid package for Ukraine, with a decision on its approval expected before the end of 2026.

Türkiye’s inflation progress helps stabilize banking sector despite regional shocks: S&P Global
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:29:12 UTC
02:29:12 KST

Emirhan Yilmaz and Emir Yildirim
23 October 2026•Update: 23 October 2026
The Turkish banking system is facing a series of global and regional economic shocks, but the economic administration’s disinflation process and the economic outlook appear “better than anticipated,” with an S&P Global Ratings financial director describing the situation as “manageable.”
S&P Global gathered leading representatives, firms, and financial institutions at the Türkiye Capital Markets Conference 2026 in Istanbul on Thursday.
Regina Argenio, director of financial institutions at S&P Global, told Anadolu that the risks Türkiye’s banking system is facing are “meaningful.”
“But because of the progress that we are seeing in terms of disinflation, and because the economy is ending up better than what we were anticipating at the beginning of the war in (the) Middle East, we do think that the situation is manageable," she said.
Argenio noted that S&P Global is monitoring the ability of Turkish banks to continue successfully rolling over their substantial external debt, warning that any disruptions on this front could prove problematic, while emphasizing that the removal of all regulatory deferral measures implemented over the past year has been a positive step ensuring stability.
She stated that increasing credit volume is a difficult process given the high real interest rates that banks are dealing with now, which have led to a decline in lending.
“It could be better next year if the rates are cut, and we see this transmission into the pricing, to the loans, we might see positive development there,” she said.
“And it's more difficult for the SMEs and the retail customer to afford such extremely high level of cost of financing, and that's where we see the bucket of potential risk coming from the banking sector, in terms of asset quality deterioration going forward,” she added.
Argenio noted that net interest margins are expected to improve next year and that lower rates would result in better funding costs for the Turkish lira-denominated banking sector.
She mentioned that funding costs in foreign currencies could increase due to interest rate dynamics, while the outcome will depend on the timing and pace of rate cuts, as well as the result of the disinflation program.
“Going forward, if the country is able to sustainably reduce inflation and increase confidence into the economy and therefore produce a stronger economic growth, more resilient, more stable economic environment -- in terms of foreign exchange risk -- that could be a meaningful improvement in terms of asset quality for the banking sector, particularly if you look at the real profitability. Because nominal-wise, you might see some decline. But, in real terms, if things goes in the right direction, we could see better profitability. So, the return on the capital should improve in (the) real term,” she said.
Argenio stated that the impact of the recent fund probes in Türkiye would remain limited if it were an isolated issue, but the policy response has been strong so far.
She noted that the liquidity provided to the banking sector helped contain the impact, adding that “it’s early to say” what the impact will be on the cost of external borrowing.
“There could also be a small component of higher cost of risk that the Turkish borrower will have to pay going forward — it depends on how much contained and how quickly the situation is managed internally,” she added.

US consumer sentiment hits a near-record low before midterm elections
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
17:26:21 UTC
02:26:21 KST

US consumer sentiment hits a near-record low before midterm elections
Independent voters’ economic anxieties highlight political implications of plummeting US consumer sentiment.
Consumer sentiment in the United States hit a near-record low in the final reading before the consequential midterm elections as cost-of-living issues weigh on US consumers.
The University of Michigan’s Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped on Friday as continuing tensions between the US and Iran drove up prices at the grocery store and the petrol pump.
The reading dropped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September, leading to the second-lowest reading on record. The lowest was only a few months ago in May, when it stood at 44.8 points.
The report measures how consumers feel about their personal finances at present and how they expect it will change over the next 12 months; whether they feel it is a good time to make major household purchases; and their expectations for the US economy over the next 12 months, as well as five years.
“Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy,” said Joanne Hsu, the director of the Surveys of Consumers. “Sentiment is now 10 percent below a year ago and 15 percent less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict.”
Political pressure
Crucially, weaker sentiment was fuelled by self-identified political independents. The group’s sentiment dropped to 42.4 points, slightly above the all-time low of 40.6 points, which it reached in May.
Since January, the number of independents pointing to inflation pressures hurting their financial situation rose by 27 percent. Republicans referencing the same issue rose by 52 percent, and the figure rose by 15 percent among Democrats.
Households with no or limited exposure to the stock market — which until recently had been soaring on enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence investment boom — have also cited high prices as a drag on their finances more frequently than at the start of the year.
Consumers’ expectations for inflation over the next five years rose to 3.5 percent from 3.4 percent in September and 3.2 percent in March.
“Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year’s increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum,” Hsu wrote. “The fact that aggregate consumer spending has been relatively resilient despite negative views of the economy provides another reason for caution. If part of consumption currently reflects precautionary spending to avoid future price hikes, disinflation may be even more difficult to achieve.”
The sentiment comes amid heightened prices for consumers. Inflation rose by 3.7 percent year on year last week, according to the recent consumer price index report, and petrol prices remain high, although lower than a month ago.
The average price for a gallon of petrol is $4.29 ($1.13 per litre) on Friday, down from $4.47 ($1.18 per litre) this time last month, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks daily petrol prices.
Friday’s report comes in advance of the final monetary policy decision before the midterm elections. On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve is largely expected to maintain rates at 3.75–4.00 percent after raising rates by 25 basis points in September. CME FedWatch, which tracks the likelihood of certain monetary policy decisions, forecasts an 89.5 percent chance that rates will remain unchanged.

Romania blames Russia after drone sinks ship in the Black Sea
One sailor killed and three others missing after Comoros-flagged Khoryv hit near Romanian waters.
Romania has blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off Romania’s Black Sea coast, killing one crew member and leaving three others missing.
It’s the latest drone attack targeting commercial shipping off the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria, with at least seven cargo ships hit and 30 sailors reported killed or missing in the past two weeks, raising fears of an escalation in Russia’s war against Ukraine.
The drone struck the Comoros-flagged vessel Khoryv and its crew of 13 Ukrainian and Azeri sailors on Friday, 13 nautical miles (24km) off Romania’s port of Constanta, just outside Romania’s territorial waters.
The shipping data website MarineTraffic showed the Khoryv departed Turkiye on Wednesday and was headed for Romania’s Sulina port, which links the Danube River to the Black Sea.
The canal has become the primary route for Ukrainian exporters, which rely on ports on the Danube and Romanian territorial waters, as Russia has attacked Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports.
Video released by Romanian authorities showed only a small part of the hull of the capsized tanker still visible above the waves as it sank.
Romania launched a rescue operation after the Khoryv sent a distress signal about 10am local time (0700 GMT).

Drone attack surge in the Black Sea
