Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators to meet in Abu Dhabi, says Zelensky
- Ukraine, Russia and the US plan technical peace talks in Abu Dhabi in early November, with Zelensky hoping this leads to a leaders’ meeting and stronger security guarantees.
- Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to discuss a full ceasefire, or limited deals on energy or maritime issues, while stressing Europe should join the talks and territory remains a leaders’ issue.
- He also said Starlink speed limits and delayed air defence interceptors are hurting Ukraine’s defence, and he criticised eased sanctions on Russia as helping Moscow continue the war.
AI generated
WASHINGTON - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct 23 that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of the countries’ leaders would follow.
Zelensky said he spoke with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Oct 23 after their meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier this week.
He said any peace agreement would need strong security guarantees for Ukraine and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army.
“The plan is to meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course,” Zelensky told the Hudson Institute think-tank via a video link.
He said much would depend on Russia, noting that a similar meeting expected this month had not materialised.
Zelensky stressed the importance of continued diplomatic efforts to reach a ceasefire and end the war, now in its fifth year, adding that Europe should also be involved in the talks.
The Ukrainian president said it was critical for the technical discussions to be followed by a meeting of the countries’ leaders.
He said he hoped to have another meeting with the US negotiators, adding that Ukraine was ready to start negotiating on a full ceasefire, or even an agreement covering just the energy sector, or maritime operations, if Moscow was unwilling to discuss a broader deal.
He also welcomed the return of 270 soldiers who had been captive in Russia, but said further exchanges were needed, with some Ukrainian troops held in Russia for over 12 years since Russia’s annexation of the Crimea region.
“If they want to raise any topic, we are ready, but territories is a sensitive issue which can be (addressed) during discussions on the level of leaders,” he said.
The White House had no immediate comment on the plans for a trilateral meeting at the technical level.
Ukraine’s military was still grappling with access to Starlink communications systems, Zelensky said, despite US assurances that speed restrictions had been removed.
“The speed limits on Starlink and Starshield are still there, and the speed has not been restored,” he said, contradicting a statement by US President Donald Trump that the services had been fully restored.
Zelensky said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had assured him in a phone call that the satellite communications services would be restored within 48 to 72 hours, but that had not occurred, degrading Kyiv’s ability to defend against Russian attacks.
“On the civilian sector and also closer to the frontline, we still have the same limit, 161kmh maximum, so it means 100 miles (160.9km),” he said.
The limits make it impossible for Ukraine to counter Russia’s jet-powered drones, which travel at speeds of around 450kmh, officials have said.
Ukraine was also waiting for a shipment of air defence interceptors that had been previously agreed, Zelensky said, complicating Ukrainian defensive efforts in the face of nearly daily massive attacks by Russian drones and missiles.
He expressed frustration about Western moves to relax some sanctions against Russia that he said were enabling Moscow to continue its war against Ukraine.
“Sanctions work, but total sanctions,” he said. “If you put, please put, don’t lift.”
Trump in October announced an agreement for Russia to supply diesel to the United States for the first time since 2022, and temporarily waived parts of a new US sanctions law against Russia. REUTERS

Donald Trump joked with rally-goers on Thursday evening that he had “the right to run again” for president, invoking a claim he has repeatedly made that he may seek a third term despite it being unconstitutional.
“I don’t know who is going to be your next president and I think the law said, I’m not 100% sure, but I think the law says I’m not allowed to run again,” Trump said in Sioux City, Iowa.
Trump went on to seemingly acknowledge that the 22nd amendment prohibits presidents from seeking a third term but then invoked his familiar false claims that Democrats “stole” the 2020 presidential election from him.
“Well, the one thing is different: they cheated us on the second one because we won it three times. So I think I have the right to run again,” Trump said, laughing.
“I think I have the right to run again because they cheated,” Trump added with a coy smile, drawing applause from the crowd.
Trump has consistently teased that he will run again for president, which would be a direct violation of the US constitution.
In October 2025, Trump told reporters he “would love” to run for a third term. At a rally in Texas in February, the president told the crowd, “Maybe we should do one more term,” claiming he was “entitled” to it.
Last year, the Trump store started selling “Trump 2028” hats. The US president went as far as to wear one during the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in July.
His allies have dismissed the president’s claims as a joke.
Mike Johnson, the speaker of the House, told reporters last year that Trump “has a good time with that, trolling the Democrats” with claims of a third term. Johnson said he didn’t see a way to amend the constitution to allow Trump to run again.
But opponents have raised concerns that Trump is being serious.
Trump himself has recognized the restrictions imposed by the US constitution.
Even during Thursday night’s rally, he said, “I’ve studied that phrase for ever. Unfortunately, it’s quite concise. There’s not a lot of wiggle room. It says something to the effect that ‘under no circumstances and for any reason will you even consider thinking about running for president if you had – ’.”
The president, who enjoys wide support thanks to his loyal Maga base, has urged supporters to vote as though he is on the ballot in November’s US midterm elections to help Republicans pick up more seats. The impact of this unconventional strategy remains to be seen as Trump’s approval ratings fall to new lows.

Inside the legal design of America's Russia sanctions U-turn
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:18:12 UTC
01:18:12 KST

Inside the legal design of America's Russia sanctions U-turn
Vladimir Putin (L) and U.S. President Donald Trump (R) arrive for a group photo at the G20 Summit in Osaka, Japan on June 28, 2019. (Brendan Smialowski/AFP via Getty Images)
Ieva Miyares
Independent consultant on illicit finance, anti-corruption, and governance
The first Russian diesel tanker under the new deal between Russia and the United States is now heading for New York with a 40,000-metric-ton cargo, enough to cover barely two hours of American demand.
The deal began with a phone call, in which Russian President Vladimir Putin seems to have persuaded his U.S. counterpart, President Donald Trump, that Russian diesel could ease the energy prices he blamed on Ukraine's strikes.
And the argument appears to have landed. Within a week, Washington had reversed its policy, agreed to a diesel deal, issued a Treasury license opening global markets to Russian diesel, and waived the Graham Act sanctions on Russia's largest oil buyers.
Each step was presented as relief for Americans facing high fuel prices. Beyond the deal's potential electoral dividends for Trump, the legal architecture of these measures tells another story, one that deserves just as much attention.
President Trump has certified to Congress that the waiver serves the U.S. national interest, but has not publicly explained how. What both decisions do is reopen markets, revenue, and payment channels for Moscow, which has secured them without a ceasefire or any other concession to Ukraine.
Anatomy of General License 135
The diesel deal rests on a Treasury license, General License 135, issued on Oct. 9, which lifts U.S. sanctions on Russian diesel imposed in 2014 and 2022. Because those sanctions were set by presidential order, the president could likely lift them, though arguably only after notifying Congress.
What stands out is the license design, which does far more for Moscow than for the Americans it was meant to help. Unlike earlier licenses, which lasted 30 days and covered only cargoes already at sea, GL 135 covers Russian diesel sold anywhere in the world until April 2027, giving Russian exporters six months to supply both existing and new buyers.
Another aspect is that the license covers only diesel. That might reflect its importance to U.S. voters, but it also allows Russia an opening in one of its most valuable export markets, which has been recently targeted by Ukraine.
Who benefits
For American consumers, the gains are limited: the promised volumes equal less than two weeks of U.S. demand. Moreover, the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022 still bans Russian energy imports into the U.S. until Ukraine accepts the peace agreement, a condition that has not been met.
Thus, the potential U.S. diesel importers who would rely on the license risk civil penalties up to the value of their cargo and the forfeiture of their ships, which a presidential pardon cannot cancel. With so much at stake, few importers are likely to take that risk, which may explain why Trump presents the deal as supply for "the American and Global Marketplace."
The 2022 import ban applies only to the U.S., so the diesel will go to buyers in the global markets.
There, the license lets traders, shippers and banks handle Russian diesel and take dollar payments without breaching U.S. sanctions, and the proceeds go to Russia’s oil companies.
Meanwhile, Kyiv is under pressure from Washington, which reportedly urged Ukraine to stop striking Russian refineries, the same facilities that now supply the diesel its license has brought back to market.
The Graham Act waiver
In September, Trump signed the Lindsey Graham Act, a law targeting the five largest buyers of Russian energy and entities involved in oil sanctions evasion, which many analysts took as a sign of a tougher line on Russia.
Its main weapon was a tariff of up to 100% on goods from Russia’s biggest energy buyers: China, India and Turkey, which have bought about half, 37% and 5% of its crude exports since late 2022. However, on Oct. 16, two days before these measures were due to take effect, and only a month after signing the act, Trump waived them.
As with the license, the waiver may do little for Americans and a great deal for Russia and its biggest customers.
The sanctions package was designed to push these buyers away from Russian crude oil, which could have driven global oil prices up in the short term. Over time, however, the expectation within the G7 was that other producers would likely fill the gap, leaving Russia with fewer customers, at steeper discounts, and with less income to fund the war.
After the signed waiver, the benefit to American consumers is yet to be seen, while Moscow's revenue will be immediate.
Moreover, the benefits to Moscow extend far beyond its oil customers.
Besides tariffs, the Graham Act aimed to pressure every stage of its oil trade: the shadow fleet, the ports and insurers, state banks such as Sberbank, VTB and Gazprombank, and the Central Bank. Nearly all of this is now on hold. Existing U.S. sanctions on those banks remain, but the waiver gives up the act's reach to the foreign ports, insurers and banks Russia relies on to evade sanctions. In September 2026, Russian-flagged "shadow" tankers more than doubled year on year, carrying 36% of the shadow fleet's oil and making Russia the most common flag in the shadow fleet.
The cost to credibility
The wider cost is the loss of credibility of U.S. sanctions globally.
Washington has pressured India and China to buy less Russian oil by adding an extra 25% tariff on Indian goods, which was later withdrawn.
The Graham Act was meant to fill that gap and write these secondary tariffs into a law. The waiver shows that U.S. sanctions are less a firm commitment and can shift after a phone call.
Traders in the Gulf, Turkey and Asia, and the shadow fleet may now face lighter compliance requirements, making it cheaper for Russia to reach and sell in the global markets.
The same logic applies to banks and insurers: those that have avoided Russian business may now be more willing to reconsider, potentially allowing Russian money back into the financial system. Meanwhile, the EU, the U.K. and G7 partners still enforce their sanctions, leaving their firms barred from trade that U.S.-linked competitors can now pursue.
A pause or a new direction?
The past week has brought a marked shift in U.S. policy towards Russia and Ukraine.
Over the same period, there were reports of threats to U.S. intelligence sharing and disruptions to Starlink in Ukraine. The moves have drawn rare bipartisan criticism, but it is not yet clear whether that will change anything.
The law may offer firmer ground than politics. Lawmakers argue the diesel license conflicts with the 2022 import ban, which could invite a legal challenge. Some have also called for limits on the president's waiver power. Whether Congress acts will show if it is willing to defend the sanctions it wrote.
The question is whether this is a temporary detour or a new direction.
Pressure from Congress, from European allies, or from Kyiv itself could still pull Washington back towards its earlier policy of backing Ukraine against its aggressor. The deal may settle the matter on its own if it delivers neither lower prices nor progress towards peace; however, ultimately at a major cost to Ukraine and U.S. credibility.
Editor's note: The opinions expressed in the op-ed section are those of the authors and do not purport to reflect the views of the Kyiv Independent.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said that Israel’s daily violations of the ceasefire in Gaza undermine trust in the international system and create an atmosphere of distrust.
Speaking at the opening of the 9th Istanbul Mediation Conference on Friday, Fidan said occupation in Gaza and the occupied West Bank continues and is met with impunity.
He stressed that ensuring humanitarian aid access and protecting children in particular must be priorities, reiterating that the Israel-Palestine conflict can only be resolved through a “just political solution.”
Dialogue and mutual trust
Fidan said Türkiye’s mediation efforts rest on the consent of the parties, mutual trust and inclusiveness, citing Ankara’s engagement in Libya.
“Türkiye's efforts in Libya, for instance, show how consent, mutual trust, and inclusiveness can build confidence,” he said.
“We engage in a result-oriented dialogue in Libya with all parties, both in the West and the East, as well as international partners,” the foreign minister said.
A Libyan-owned process based on sincere dialogue is the only path to a lasting solution, he said.
Fidan stressed that communication channels must remain open even when progress is slow and fragile. That approach, he said, has guided Türkiye’s efforts in Russia-Ukraine talks, the Black Sea grain initiative, as well as the Ankara process between Somalia and Ethiopia.
Regional ownership
Turning to the recently signed Mecca defence agreement between Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, Fidan said the alliance “aims to secure the region's peace, prosperity and future”.
“Its foundation in regional ownership gives these efforts a stronger chance of success,” he noted.
He also highlighted the Balkans Peace Platform as a mechanism rooted in regional ownership that could turn dialogue among Balkan nations into practical results.
Fidan stressed that Türkiye has consistently worked to elevate mediation from a diplomatic instrument into a strategic discipline, and built the institutional architecture to match that ambition.
“We do not seek to impose outcomes, but to create the conditions in which parties can reach their own,” he said.
“Because mediation is not about deciding who wins, who loses, or who makes concessions. It is about finding common ground and working towards a win-win solution for all parties.”
Türkiye's experience, based on sincere dialogue, sustained engagement, and regional ownership, demonstrated how this approach can contribute to regional and global security, Fidan added.

Experts highlight Lut Desert geopark bid, Kerman’s geological and natural attractions
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:16:42 UTC
01:16:42 KST

Experts highlight Lut Desert geopark bid, Kerman’s geological and natural attractions
TEHRAN - Experts have highlighted the potential benefits of establishing a UNESCO Global Geopark in Iran’s Lut Desert, saying the initiative could promote sustainable tourism, create local jobs and strengthen protection of the region’s unique geological heritage.
The issue was discussed at a specialized meeting on the Lut Desert, part of a series of seminars on Kerman studies held at Shahid Bahonar University of Kerman.
Speaking at the meeting on Thursday, Ebrahim Mohammadi, a faculty member at the The Graduate University of Advanced Technology (GUAT) in Kerman, discussed the province’s tourism potential, with a particular focus on the Kaluts of Shahdad, a striking landscape of eroded earth formations in the Lut Desert.
Mohammadi said Kerman province is home to 10 properties inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List and covers an area larger than the combined territories of 115 countries. He didn’t, however, mention that some of those UNESCO sites are shared with other nearby provinces.
Despite its vast size and exceptional range of natural, geological, historical, cultural, religious and spiritual attractions, the province attracts only about 0.7% of Iran’s tourists, although it accounts for around 11% of the country’s territory, he said.
Mohammadi, who holds a doctorate in paleontology, outlined several potential benefits of securing Global Geopark status for the Lut Desert.
He said the designation could strengthen the desert’s international profile and bring its important geological sites under a more integrated management framework.
It could also encourage sustainable geotourism, support the development of scientific and nature-based tourism routes, and persuade visitors to spend more time in the region by offering a wider range of experiences.
According to Mohammadi, the initiative could generate employment and strengthen the local economy by creating opportunities for tour guides, traditional accommodation providers, transport services, handicraft producers and other local businesses.
He also emphasized the importance of expanding scientific research and education, particularly in geology and geomorphology, while increasing local communities’ participation in protecting the region’s natural heritage and benefiting from tourism.
Elsewhere in his remarks, Mohammadi suggested that a geopark could help improve conservation across the Lut Desert by establishing stronger management links among its prominent geological sites and reducing damage caused by uncontrolled tourism and inappropriate use of natural resources.
Developing a unified tourism destination would also help promote the Kaluts of Shahdad alongside other geological attractions through complementary routes and visitor experiences, he added.
The initiative could further strengthen Kerman’s international tourism brand, raise awareness of its natural and geological assets, and expand scientific and international cooperation.
Mohammadi also stressed that sustainable development in the region would depend on directing tourism toward environmental protection, distributing its economic benefits among local communities and adopting scientific and participatory management practices.
He also highlighted the need for a comprehensive conservation and tourism plan, systematic documentation of geological sites, public education and cooperation between responsible institutions and local residents.
The meeting also addressed the historical importance of traditional water-management systems in Shahdad, a settlement on the edge of the Lut Desert.
Mohammad Barshan, director of Kerman province’s Qanat Center, discussed the origins and age of Shahdad’s qanats and their role in supplying water for agriculture and sustaining human settlement in the arid region.
Qanats are traditional underground water channels that transport groundwater to the surface, allowing communities to obtain water in areas where rainfall is scarce.
Drawing on years of research and practical experience with qanats, Barshan emphasized their significance in the development of settlements and civilizations.
“Digging a qanat is an epic, a great epic of replacing death with life,” he said, describing the ancient water systems as closely linked to the development of civilization among communities across Iran.
Barshan also discussed the qanats of Shahdad, stressing the central role of water in the rise and decline of civilizations.
“Civilizations are formed with water and disappear with water,” he said.
The discussions highlighted the potential for combining geological conservation, scientific research and the preservation of traditional water-management heritage to support sustainable tourism and local development in Kerman province.

LIAA strengthens ties between Latvian entrepreneurs and Swedish investors during crown princess Victoria’s visit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:14:56 UTC
01:14:56 KST

During the visit of Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden to Latvia, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) organised a meeting between Latvian women entrepreneurs and Swedish female investors on 21 October to discuss access to finance and business growth. On the same day, LIAA Director Ieva Jāgere met the Crown Princess at a roundtable discussion entitled “Women in Business” at the Stockholm School of Economics in Riga. Both events focused on women’s entrepreneurship, talent development and opportunities for cooperation between Latvia and Sweden.
LIAA Brings Together Women Entrepreneurs to Discuss Investment and Growth
At the LIAA Lounge, Latvian women entrepreneurs met with Lisen Oliw, Partner at the venture capital fund BackingMinds, and Michaela Berglund, Founder of Feminvest. The meeting was moderated by LIAA Director Ieva Jāgere.
“Gender equality is part of the cultural fabric of Nordic societies. In business, it must also be reflected in opportunities to access capital and turn ideas into reality. We have talented women with experience in leading teams, developing products and operating in international markets. I want to see more of this expertise and ambition translated into internationally successful women-owned businesses.
“For Swedish investors, Latvia offers capable teams and companies with growth potential, while partnerships can provide our entrepreneurs with capital, market knowledge and access to new customers. LIAA helps identify the right partners to turn these ambitions into reality,” emphasised Ieva Jāgere, Director of the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA).
The meeting brought together representatives of Latvian companies and startups from various sectors: Egija Gailuma (Engycell), Anna Ramata-Stunda (Alternative Plants), Elza Priede (StartSchool), Anna Gabuniya (L-Blend), Jekaterina Romanova (PrintyMed), Solvita Kostjukova (P-Agro Minerals) and Laura Sičevska (Smart Indicators).
The participants presented their businesses, growth ambitions and interest in the Swedish market. In discussions with investors, they explored business models, financing requirements and their companies’ investment readiness. Beyond access to capital, the participants highlighted the value of investors’ expertise and international networks in helping businesses attract new customers and establish partnerships.
BackingMinds is a female-founded venture capital fund that seeks promising companies and founders beyond traditional investor networks, including women entrepreneurs whose business potential may previously have been overlooked.
Feminvest, meanwhile, promotes women’s participation in investing and invests in women-owned businesses through its fund. Both investors’ approaches create opportunities for entrepreneurs seeking financing and strategic partners to support further growth.
“Latvia needs more venture capital funds that invest in our companies and help them expand internationally. Access to financing at both early and growth stages remains insufficient. We have many experienced women leaders, but management experience alone does not guarantee access to capital for developing their own businesses.
“That is why investors who actively seek out women-founded companies and recognise their potential are particularly valuable. Through meetings like this, we help Latvian entrepreneurs gain visibility among these investors,” said Vita Balode-Andrūsa, Director of LIAA’s Export and Innovation Services Department.
Ieva Jāgere Meets Crown Princess Victoria at Women in Business Roundtable
LIAA was represented at the “Women in Business” roundtable discussion at the Stockholm School of Economics in Riga by Director Ieva Jāgere and Director of the Export and Innovation Services Department Vita Balode-Andrūsa.
During the event, Ieva Jāgere met Her Royal Highness Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden. Representatives from the business, financial and public sectors discussed opportunities for women to develop businesses and fully utilise their knowledge and talents.
In her address, the Crown Princess emphasised the importance of education in developing talent and future leaders, noting that no society can fully realise its potential when opportunities are unequal. She highlighted gender equality as a foundation of democratic society that also contributes to a stronger economy.
“I welcome the Crown Princess’s emphasis on the connection between talent development, equal opportunities and economic growth. Investment in education delivers greater returns when women can fully apply their knowledge — leading businesses, creating innovations and bringing entrepreneurial ideas to life,” said LIAA Director Ieva Jāgere.
The Crown Princess also acknowledged Latvia’s and Sweden’s achievements in women’s representation in management positions, while stressing that challenges remain.
The two countries’ strong positions are reflected in Eurostat data. In 2024, women held 44.4% of managerial positions in Sweden and 43.4% in Latvia — the two highest shares in the European Union, where the average proportion of women in management was 35.2%.
Latvian Expertise and Swedish Capital: Opportunities for Joint Growth
During the roundtable discussion, Ieva Tetere, Chairwoman of the Management Board of SEB Bank, highlighted the opportunity to combine the expertise and growth ambitions of Latvia’s highly educated professionals with Swedish capital.
Anastasija Oļeiņika, President and Head of Platform at the global e-commerce and technology company FYUL, emphasised the importance of Swedish experience and financing in supporting Latvian innovators and startups.
Lisen Oliw, Partner at BackingMinds, pointed to growing interest among Swedish investors in the Baltic region and positively assessed the support available in Latvia for business development and acceleration. Such initiatives help international investors discover Latvian companies and identify potential investment opportunities.
Michaela Berglund, Founder of Feminvest, drew attention to the importance of joint Latvian-Swedish policy initiatives in encouraging investment.
The discussion also included a call to view the Baltic and Nordic countries as a single, interconnected business and investment region, strengthening cross-border investment and cooperation in innovation.

Spouses of six countries’ ambassadors named honorary tourism envoys of Hamadan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:14:15 UTC
01:14:15 KST

Spouses of six countries’ ambassadors named honorary tourism envoys of Hamadan
TEHRAN - The spouses of ambassadors from Denmark, Romania, Mexico, Uruguay, Nicaragua and Armenia, along with Romania’s ambassador to Iran, have been named honorary ambassadors for cultural heritage, tourism and handicrafts in Iran’s western province of Hamadan.
The initiative, held in cooperation with Iran’s Foreign Ministry, aims to introduce Hamadan’s historical and cultural attractions to international audiences and strengthen cultural ties and tourism cooperation between Iran and other countries.
Speaking at the ceremony on Wednesday, Mohammadreza Akbari, head of the Hamadan Department of Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts, said cultural heritage could transcend geographical borders, linguistic differences and national identities, serving as a common language that brings nations closer together.
He described Hamadan as a province with thousands of years of history, valuable historical monuments, rich cultural traditions and considerable potential in tourism and handicrafts.
Akbari said these assets form part of Iran’s civilizational identity and the shared heritage of humanity, adding that introducing them to international audiences could improve mutual understanding and pave the way for greater cultural and tourism cooperation.
According to Akbari, cooperation with diplomatic figures could help introduce foreign audiences to the province’s historical landmarks, local arts, handicrafts and cultural traditions.
He also emphasized that developing international tourism requires more than historical monuments and natural attractions, noting that effective promotion, sustained international engagement and cooperation between cultural and tourism institutions are equally important.
Akbari expressed hope that the initiative would mark the beginning of lasting cooperation between Hamadan and the six countries, contributing to cultural understanding, friendly relations and the preservation of shared human heritage.
Hamadan, often described as the historical and civilizational capital of Iran, is home to a range of archaeological, historical and natural attractions.
Among its best-known sites are the ancient city of Ecbatana, the Ganjnameh inscriptions and waterfall, Ali Sadr Cave, the mausoleums of Avicenna and Baba Taher, and the Alavian Dome, to name a few.
The province is also home to Lalejin, internationally recognized for its pottery-making tradition, which has made it one of Iran’s leading handicrafts centers.

Beyza Binnur Donmez
23 October 2026•Update: 23 October 2026
Switzerland on Friday expressed concern over statements by several parties to the conflict calling for violence or escalation amid rising tensions in the occupied West Bank.
A spokesperson for the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA) told Anadolu in a statement that Switzerland was calling on all sides to exercise "maximum restraint" and avoid steps that could further intensify violence.
Bern is "concerned by statements from several parties to the conflict calling for violence or escalation," the statement said.
Asked about reports that Israel was preparing for a possible closure of the entire occupied West Bank following a shooting attack near Hebron, the FDFA said: "Any security measures must be proportionate and respect international law, including international humanitarian law and human rights law."
"As the occupying power, Israel is obligated to protect the civilian population and guarantee access to essential services and humanitarian aid," it added.
The spokesperson also expressed concern over violence in the Hebron area ahead of Israeli elections and condemned attacks against civilians and security forces.
The Israeli army claimed Friday that two soldiers had been killed and three others seriously wounded in a shooting attack in Hebron, a city in the southern occupied West Bank.
The army's statement came hours after two Palestinians were killed in a shootout with Israeli forces following allegations that they had opened fire at Israeli occupiers in Hebron, wounding five.
Following the reported shooting, the Israeli army announced a full closure of Hebron and several surrounding towns.
The occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, has witnessed an escalation in Israeli military operations and occupier attacks since Israel launched its genocidal war on the Gaza Strip in October 2023.
The attacks have included the killing and arrest of Palestinians, the demolition of homes and other structures, the burning of mosques and vehicles, the destruction of agricultural land, farmers being prevented from accessing their fields, and the displacement of Palestinian communities, alongside illegal settlement expansion.

Gold falls below $4,000 for 1st time since July
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:12:58 UTC
01:12:58 KST

Gokhan Ergocun
23 October 2026•Update: 23 October 2026
Gold prices fell below the $4,000 level for the first time since July 2026 as a selloff in technology stocks and inflation concerns fueled by rising oil prices weighed on demand.
Gold traded at $3,998 an ounce, down 0.5% as of 1600GMT. The precious metal has fallen 6.3% over the past month and 2.63% over the past year.
Silver prices also fell 0.75% to $54.2 per ounce.
The decline came as losses in technology and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks prompted investors to sell precious metals to cover losses elsewhere in their portfolios.
Concerns over the cost of AI investment intensified after Meta Platforms outlined plans to increase capital expenditure, raising fears that technology companies could take on additional debt to finance their expansion.
Rising oil prices also pressured gold by heightening inflation concerns and reinforcing expectations that interest rates could remain elevated for longer.
Higher interest rates typically reduce the appeal of gold, which pays no interest, relative to interest-bearing assets.
However, uncertainty over the sustainability of AI investment, a key contributor to US economic growth, prompted markets to pare back expectations for further Federal Reserve rate increases, offering some support to precious metals.

Elon Musk Just Dumped Another $76 Million Into the Midterms
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:12:49 UTC
01:12:49 KST

Elon Musk gave his personal political committee, America PAC, more than $76 million in the first two weeks of October to boost Republicans in the final stretch of the midterms, according to a pre-election report the PAC filed Thursday evening with the Federal Election Commission.
The group spent nearly $43 million in the first two weeks of October, and entered the campaign’s last leg holding nearly $47 million in cash.
The Texas Senate race dominated the new spending. It drew $15.2 million, double what the PAC spent there all summer. That spending included $12.4 million to attack Democratic candidate James Talarico and $2.8 million to promote Republican Ken Paxton.
Daily filings since then show $9.1 million more against Talarico, bringing the PAC’s spending against him this cycle to nearly $28 million, about 40 percent of everything it has spent supporting or opposing candidates. The PAC also shifted toward online ads, spending $11.4 million on digital ads in the same two weeks, which is close to what it spent on mail and texting combined.
All told, Musk has given more than $445 million to Republican political groups this election cycle, according to WIRED’s analysis of FEC filings, making him the biggest known individual donor in the midterms. More than $165 million of that has gone to America PAC since July alone.
America PAC declined to comment.
Musk—who has several companies, including Tesla and SpaceX, based in Texas—has also been posting online about the race. On Wednesday, Musk posted on X that “there is something deeply wrong with Talarico,” then called him “a creep” and claimed, without evidence, that he “would vote to take away your kids and transition them.” Earlier this month, Musk amplified a false claim that Talarico had been treated at a mental health facility. Talarico shot back the same day: “There is something deeply wrong with a political system that allows one trillionaire to buy his own personal US Senator.”
The Texas race remains a toss-up. An Emerson College poll of 1,000 likely Texas voters, conducted October 17 to 19, found Talarico at 48 percent and Paxton at 46 percent, within the poll’s 3-point margin of error.
The stakes for Musk reach well beyond Texas. If Democrats win the House, the lawmakers in line to lead its committees have signaled they will investigate his role in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), his companies’ federal contracts, and what Zoe Lofgren, a California Democrat, called an “astounding” number of conflicts of interest. Unified Democratic control of Congress would pose even more problems for him.
Silicon Valley Democrats added another target on Friday: restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite service in Ukraine. In a letter to the White House demanding an investigation, Representatives Sam Liccardo, Jimmy Panetta, and Ro Khanna vowed that the next Congress “will closely scrutinize federal funding awarded to Mr. Musk’s businesses.”

UN chief race enters decisive phase as new contender arrives
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:12:26 UTC
01:12:26 KST

UAE’s star diplomat Lana Nusseibeh has entered the race for the UN secretary-general position, challenging front-runner Rebeca Grynspan at a decisive time for the global organisation's future. The UN chief race could now lead to the first ever female secretary-general.
As the race to elect the next UN Secretary-General enters its final phase, former Costa Rican Vice President Rebeca Grynspan retains a challenging lead, but a new contender is emerging, as UAE Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh announced her candidacy this week.
The growing excitement around the race is also fueled by the prospect of a female UN secretary-general, something that has never happened in the UN's more than 80-year history.
As part of a complex election process, an informal straw poll of officials in the deciding United Nations Security Council last week gave Grynspan a narrow lead over her closest competitors: Guyana’s former Foreign Minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett and Argentina’s International Atomic Energy Agency Director-General Rafael Grossi.
But after receiving two opposing votes the race has been relaunched allowing new candidates to participate.
The winner needs at least nine votes from the 15-member UN Security Council without opposition from any of the five permanent members — the US, the UK, France, China and Russia — and they have until the end of December to choose the successor to current UN chief Antonio Gutteres, before the UN General Assembly confirms the appointment.
Campaigning alongside Grynspan, Grossi and Rodrigues-Birkett are former Ecuadorian Foreign Minister Maria Fernanda Espinosa, former Senegalese President Macky Sall, former UN Under-Secretary-General Olara Otunnu of Uganda, and Ecuadorian diplomat Ivonne A-Baki.
UAE’s Nusseibeh announced as fresh contender
Senior UAE diplomat and UAE Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh energised the race when her nomination was announced this week, known for her versatility in “quiet diplomacy” in the campaign for peace and for creating space for wider political settlements.
Launching her candidacy, Nusseibeh said, “I have spent much of my professional life working in and around the United Nations, and I have seen first-hand what determined diplomacy can achieve - countries with profound differences finding common ground, and agreement where people said agreement was impossible.”
In her vision statement, she puts peace and security at the core while also promising to deliver across the board on development and human rights, as well as reform the organisation around focus and results.
"I am standing to be secretary-general because I believe this is a moment to act with greater urgency: to act earlier, bring people together across difference, and drive the work forward until it produces concrete results," she said.
“I wish to offer myself to this office as I would serve it: speaking frankly with every government and answering to none.”
A highly regarded diplomat who grew up between Abu Dhabi and the UK in a family of well-known political figures, Nusseibeh previously served as the UAE ambassador to the UN and is credited with elevating the UAE's profile during that time.
Nusseibeh, 48, who led the UAE’s successful bid for a Security Council seat, said that several countries approached her during the last UN General Assembly and urged her to stand.
“It's recognised today that we need someone who offers generational change for the organisation,” she said.
During the country’s 2022 to 2023 term, Nusseibeh secured the adoption of Resolution 2720, which opened the way for humanitarian aid deliveries into Gaza. A Hebrew speaker, she said she secured support for the resolution by arranging visits from Council members to the Rafah border crossing.
If she succeeds, Nusseibeh would become the first woman to lead the United Nations since its establishment in 1945, the first of Palestinian descent, and the second Secretary-General from the Arabic-speaking world after Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
“I think it would be great if the next secretary-general is a woman, but I am not running because I am a woman, I am running because I am stubbornly optimistic about the future of the United Nations and I believe we need someone who is relentless in the pursuit of diplomacy to open doors,” Nusseibeh said on Wednesday.
Grynspan holds a challenging lead
Costa Rica's former Vice President Rebeca Grynspan, 70, was born to Jewish parents who fled Poland before World War II, and she has built a Jewish family ever since. She lost her grandparents in the Holocaust after they decided to remain in Poland.
In a May interview with Euronews, Grynspan said, “I know exactly what wars take away from you and what peace allows you to do.”
“I am a generation that have lived in peace. I have never experienced war directly. But millions of people in the world today live in war zones, in conflict. And that is why I am running, because I know the difference, what peace and opportunity can do for you and your family,” she told Euronews.
Currently Secretary-General of the UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD), Grynspan said she agreed with US President Donald Trump’s “constructive” criticism that “the UN has great potential, but it's not living up to that potential,” and that a reformed UN can make a difference.
Grynspan told Euronews how she believes that in our multipolar world “the choice is if we will have multipolarity with multilateralism that bears the promise of prosperity and cooperation, or if we will have multipolarity without multilateralism that will lead us to fragmentation into a world that will be more unstable, more prone to conflict, and less prosper.”
“So we need to create again these spaces. For the convergence of divergent interests,” she added.
On the other hand, she also hailed the “amazing things that are happening in the world: you look at technology and you look at the digital world, the artificial intelligence, what is happening in medicine and in science.”
“You see those breakthroughs that you can bring to the people on the ground, to the millions of people that have right now no opportunity, that live in poverty, in absolute destitution or in hunger.“
“And you know that the world is developing really the capacity, the possibility for everybody to have a dignified life. That will depend on us. It will depend on our choices,” Grynspan explained in an interview for Euronews.
She said that the UN election race was “not like a business-as-usual type of election.”
“Conflicts in the world are going up. Trust between the countries, but also in the multilateral system, is going down. And time is running out," Grynspan told Euronews as she presented the vision of her candidacy to become the new UN secretary-general.
"So this is a moment in which we have to raise to the challenge to bring cooperation, solidarity, the principles of the UN Charter again into the center of the agenda,” she concluded.

Ukraine customs, WTO launch joint audit in Lviv region to fight corruption
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
19:12:23 EEST
01:12:23 KST

The State Customs Service of Ukraine, together with experts from the World Customs Organization (WCO), has begun reviewing internal goods-clearance procedures and is introducing the European practice of process mapping to eliminate corruption risks.
According to a statement on the State Customs Service's Telegram channel, the mapping method involves a detailed analysis of every stage of a work process, from the sequence of actions and decision-making to the allocation of powers and responsibilities among participants. This makes it possible to identify vulnerable stages and develop mechanisms to minimize the associated risks.
The practical stage of risk assessment and analysis of the actual movement of cargo took place directly at Lviv Customs facilities. During the review, WCO experts and Ukrainian customs officers assessed each stage of export and import clearance operations, as well as the use of scanners and other technical customs control equipment to eliminate the human factor.
In addition, the State Customs Service is working with WCO specialists to develop a Code of Ethics establishing standards of professional conduct and integrity for customs officers in line with international approaches.
Earlier, the State Customs Service announced the introduction of a mechanism for the automatic customs clearance of imported and exported international postal and express shipments without physically presenting them to customs authorities and without the involvement of officials.

EU trade Chief seeks to rebalance EU-China trade as Brussels weighs tougher measures
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:11:57 UTC
01:11:57 KST

The European Commission hopes to curb Chinese imports in additional sectors in upcoming talks with Beijing while exploring new trade defence measures, though the move risks triggering retaliatory action from China.
EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said on Friday that the EU was walking a tightrope in negotiations with Beijing, weighing conventional trade measures against broader political considerations.
After several months of negotiations, Brussels and Beijing reached a deal on 9 October to curb imports of hybrid cars from China. However, the agreement is unlikely to significantly narrow the EU’s record trade deficit with China, which has reached €1 billion a day, a gap the European Commission is seeking to reduce.
“There are whole sectors under threat; each head of states and government is concerned that there might be potential heavy losses of the jobs,” Šefčovič said on Friday, after a meeting of the 27 trade ministers in Ireland.
He added: “We have to proceed not only with the traditional trade techniques, but also with a very political approach, how to balance the trade between between China and the European Union.”
A new round of discussions is taking place at a technical level with Beijing until the end of the year, with political negotiation scheduled for January and March 2027.
But given the urgency, EU leaders gave the European Commission a political mandate last week to work on a “kill switch” tool that would allow Europeans to cut off China's access to their market to counter economic distortions.
Under the October deal, the EU will introduce country-specific quotas allowing 350,000 Chinese hybrid cars onto the European market annually over four years, with a fixed annual adjustment rate of 6%.
Striking a deal on new sectors
The Commission aims to extend the agreement to other sectors, but EU officials warn that progress will also depend on Beijing’s response to the EU executive’s efforts to strengthen its trade defence tools.
The Commission is set to present a new instrument on 9 October aimed at encouraging EU companies to diversify their suppliers of strategic products to reduce their dependence on China.
It also hopes to present a proposal for the so-called “kill switch” that same week and ahead of the December summit of EU leaders. Pushed by France and Germany earlier this month, it would allow the Commission to adopt radical measures against Beijing in the event of economic pressure on the EU market.
Another unilateral EU trade defence measure targeting Chinese chemicals and industrial machinery could also come in December, with the risk of prompting Chinese countermeasures.
According to the latest Chinese customs data, China's exports to the EU have continued to surge, rising by 25% over the past year.

Turkey says renewed attack on Iran would expand conflict, diplomacy only way
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23

Turkey says renewed attack on Iran would expand conflict, diplomacy only way
ISTANBUL, Oct 23 - Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan cautioned on Friday against any renewed attack on Iran, saying such a move would exacerbate tensions and further expand the conflict there, adding that diplomacy and dialogue were the only way to end the war.
Fidan met his counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy in Istanbul to discuss developments in the Iran war, attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi militants, and Russia's war in Ukraine.
It was the first collective meeting between the countries, comprising the Regional Four (R4) and EU 3 (E3), alongside Italy.
"We are all in agreement that a new attack on Iran would expand the war in the region," Fidan told a press conference after the meeting. "A military intervention on Iran is not in any way a solution. Nobody approves this at the moment," he added.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said after Friday's meetings that renewed escalation between Iran and the United States would only have losers and raise oil prices.
The comments followed a New York Times report on Wednesday that the US and Israeli militaries had drawn up specific plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the US midterm congressional election next month. Citing US officials, it said likely targets would include Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and its missile and drone arsenal.
US President Donald Trump said earlier this month that the US would not launch an attack on Iran before the midterms, as Washington and Tehran were having "productive" talks about ending their six-month-old war. On Friday, he said the US could end the war quickly but questioned whether Washington should seek a swift conclusion or allow the conflict to gradually wind down.
NATO member Turkey has been in close contact with Washington, Tehran and regional mediators to seek an end to the war. It has repeatedly called for attacks to stop and warned against the regional expansion of the conflict.
Fidan also said the countries meeting on Friday had discussed possible parameters to ensure the war in Iran does not expand further, but did not elaborate.
Following Friday's meetings, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany, France, and Britain were ready to negotiate with Iran to rule out its acquisition of nuclear weapons, while calling for support for Saudi Arabia and Yemen. REUTERS

ICE agents tackle and injure U.S. citizen student with disabilities, local officials say
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:08:06 UTC
01:08:06 KST

ICE agents tackle and injure U.S. citizen student with disabilities, local officials say
- Click here to listen to this article
-   Share via
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
- A Santa Maria High School student, who is a U.S. citizen, was detained by immigration agents on Wednesday, according to school and city officials.
- The student, a 20-year-old with limited verbal communication, was hospitalized for wrist injuries afterward.
Federal immigration agents violently detained a 20-year-old U.S. citizen and Santa Maria (Calif.) High School student with special needs on Wednesday morning, according to school and city officials.
The student, who has limited verbal communication and is on an individualized education program, was walking to school around 7 a.m. when two agents tackled him from behind, questioned him about his citizenship and restrained him in their vehicle. He was eventually released in the area where he was picked up and walked to school, where officials called for an ambulance to take him to the hospital, said Santa Maria City Councilmember Gloria Soto.
The student underwent surgery for injuries to his wrist, she said, and was left with bruises and lacerations.
Soto said a school resource officer obtained security footage from a nearby grocery store and confirmed that the people who had detained the student are agents with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
In an emailed statement, an unidentified ICE spokesperson wrote that agents were conducting a targeted enforcement operation in Santa Maria “when they encountered an individual they believed matched the description of the criminal illegal alien target.”
“When the individual resisted officers, refused lawful commands, and assumed a fighting stance with clenched fists, they relied on their training to safely control the situation until they could confirm his identity, whereupon he was released,” the spokesperson wrote.
The spokesperson added that claims that the student suffered broken bones are false because “he never requested medical assistance.”
Glenn Goldin, a retired special education teacher at Santa Maria High who still mentors the student who was detained, said he worked for a long time to build the confidence to walk by himself to school. Now he’s wary of returning to school.
The student told Goldin that he saw a black car pull up and kept walking. The agents were masked and didn’t announce who they were, but he noticed they wore vests that said “POLICE ICE.” The student told Goldin that he had his Real ID in his wallet, but the agents didn’t ask to see it.
“He told them repeatedly that the handcuffs were too tight and they were hurting him,” Goldin said.
Goldin said the student has no family and lives in a group home for adults with developmental disabilities.
After the agents released him, the student walked to school, crying and in pain. His teacher saw him and dialed 911, Goldin said.
“He was so scared,” Goldin recalled the student telling him. “He thought they were going to kill him. He thought he was going to die.”
Soto said it appears the student was racially profiled. She called for an independent investigation into how a case of mistaken identity by ICE agents ended with the student being hurt.
“Our community is living in terror right now and this needs to stop,” she said, referencing a recent uptick in immigration arrests across central California. “I’m a mother, and the thought of my child not being safe walking to school is frightening.”
The Santa Maria Police Department declined to comment and referred questions to ICE.
Alma Hernandez, board president of Santa Maria Joint Union High School District, said she was horrified by ICE’s actions.
“Our district remains committed to protecting our students and families,” she said.
Kenny Klein, the school district’s spokesperson, said the student was detained by ICE about a half-mile from campus.
“The student then proceeded to walk to school. School administration called an ambulance, and the student was taken to the hospital to receive medical care,” Klein wrote in a statement, adding that parents, guardians, students and staff were notified of the incident.
Santa Maria police responded to the situation and notified appropriate agencies, including the local district attorney and the California attorney general, he added.
805 UndocuFund, an advocacy group, wrote in an Instagram post that volunteers witnessed several more community members stopped and questioned by ICE on Wednesday. The group organized a rally and protest this Saturday in support of the student.

One killed as Elysee calls Paris area shooting ‘racist, terrorist attack’
Antiterrorism prosecutors investigating motive of attack that seriously wounded five, including a 12-year-old girl.
A gunman has killed one person and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in a possible Islamophobic “terrorist crime” in the Paris suburbs, authorities said.
An unidentified 39-year-old male suspect was taken into custody shortly after the attacks in the towns of Trappes and nearby La Verriere outside the capital on Friday.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the suspect fired at a children’s playground, a fuel station and a medical centre, the Reuters news agency reported. Three of the victims, including the 12-year-old girl, suffered life-threatening injuries, he said.
Nunez said the attack lasted less than 15 minutes and that the gunman appeared to have used “a military-grade weapon, or at least an automatic weapon”. Prosecutors were treating it as a “terrorist crime” and investigating whether it was racially or religiously motivated, he said.
The Elysee presidential palace described the shooting as a “racist, terrorist attack” as French President Emanuel Macron visited Trappes, a working-class town about 20km (13 miles) west of Paris, after the shooting on Friday.
Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh said the gunman “appeared to be firing at random and seemed intent on carrying out a massacre”.
“This was a terrorist attack with racist, likely Islamophobic, overtones,” he said.
Rabeh said the person killed was “of African origin” and that one of the wounded, who was in critical condition, was “of North African origin”.
La Verriere Mayor Nicolas Dainville said the girl, who was shot eight times, was seriously wounded but in stable condition.
“I’m North African and it’s frightening for everyone who has the same background,” Adel, a 50-year-old resident of Trappes, told the AFP news agency, saying his “heart was broken” at learning the victims might have been targeted for their race.
Two of the wounded in his town, cleaners working at a school on Friday morning when the gunman got out of his car to open fire, were of African origin, he said.
Macron said national antiterrorism prosecutors had taken over the case, opening an investigation for “murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise” and examining whether the attack targeted the “real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion” of the victims.
They said the suspect had also booby-trapped his flat with three gas canisters and electric wires “connected to a timer”.
“Our thoughts go out to the victims, their families, and all the residents of Yvelines. In this terrible ordeal, the Nation stands by their side,” Macron posted on X.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said in a post on X that the case was “very serious” and that “all resources of the security forces and the judiciary are fully mobilised”.
Tensions ahead of Saturday protests
Separately, security was tightened ahead of planned nationwide protests this weekend. Many of the demonstrations have been banned following burning and looting at protests last weekend.
Nunez said France would deploy 70,000 officers across the country on Saturday, along with helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannon. In addition, elite police units will help secure public buildings, such as city halls, in a “highly mobile” security operation, he said.
Protests last week caused chaos, with people setting fires, storming public buildings, smashing shop windows, looting and clashing with police, in France’s most violent unrest in years.
France has been on edge since the riots, and overnight curfews were put in place in cities across the country for a week.
Far-right politicians say the government has not cracked down hard enough on protesters, while left-wing groups say the security around demonstrations violates rights.
Demonstrators plan to take to the streets again on Saturday to denounce the high cost of living. Students, members of the Confederation of Labour, a national trade union and activists from the “yellow vest” movement, whose demonstrations against social injustice shook France in 2018 and 2019, are all set to join.

Ending a quarter-century-long game of hide-and-seek, CBI has arrested Satyendra Kumar
NEW DELHI: Ending a quarter-century-long game of hide-and-seek, CBI has arrested Satyendra Kumar, a key fugitive wanted in connection with Bihar’s infamous Fodder scam. The suspect had fled to Nepal and was tracked down during a train journey he took upon returning to India, the agency said.Acting on court orders, CBI had undertaken the probe into the multi-crore corruption scam involving the systematic embezzlement of funds from the Animal Husbandry Department in Bihar during the 1990s. High-profile political figures, including former Bihar chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, along with several senior bureaucrats and suppliers, have since been convicted in multiple cases related to illegal treasury withdrawals. The agency had filed dozens of FIRs to untangle a nexus of politicians, bureaucrats, suppliers and middlemen who siphoned off public funds through fake invoices for cattle feed, medicines and equipment.Kumar, alleged to be a supplier, had been on the run since 2001, vanishing into the shadows immediately after the agency filed its charge sheet in the case. His persistent failure to face trial prompted the court to issue an arrest warrant and declare him an absconder, cementing his status as one of the scam’s most elusive figures.
It was a to a manhunt that spanned more than two decades across international borders. For over 25 years, Kumar managed to evade the law by taking refuge across the border in Nepal living under an assumed identity. However, the net slowly began to tighten as CBI officials mounted human and technical surveillance to pinpoint his exact movements.The breakthrough came when intelligence revealed that Kumar had re-entered India and was travelling by train from Guna, Madhya Pradesh, to Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Acting swiftly on the input, a team was tasked with intercepting the fugitive mid-transit. Units were deployed across Lucknow Railway Station well before the train arrived. Around midnight on Oct 22, the CBI managed to take the accused into custody and placed him under arrest. He was taken to Ranchi on transit remand, where he will finally be produced before the court to face trial.
Raj Shekhar Jha is a journalist for the Times of India with over a decade of experience in reporting on national security, terrorism, crime and prisons.

Denmark rushes 50,000 cannon rounds to Ukraine to help F-16s hunt Russia’s advanced jet drones
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-23
16:07:15 UTC
01:07:15 KST

Ukraine has received more than 50,000 rounds of 20-mm ammunition from Denmark for the onboard cannons of its F-16 fighter jets, with Ukrainian pilots already using the rounds to intercept Russian jet-powered Geran attack drones, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said.
The accelerated delivery addresses a key need in Ukraine’s air defense as Russia increasingly deploys faster jet-powered drones that challenge conventional interceptors. Ukraine has also relied on F-16 cannons when stocks of air-to-air missiles are limited, making ammunition supplies important to keeping the aircraft effective against incoming aerial threats.
Denmark responds to ammunition request
The Defense Ministry thanked Denmark for responding quickly to Ukraine’s request for additional ammunition, saying the delivery directly strengthens the country’s air defenses and helps protect civilians from Russian aerial attacks.
The delivery follows a broader effort by Ukraine’s European partners to replenish F-16 cannon ammunition. On October 2, it was reported that Spain, Belgium, and Poland were also sending 20-mm rounds for Ukrainian F-16s to counter Russia’s jet-powered drones.
Belgium is also expanding its support for Ukraine’s F-16 fleet. On 16 October, Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever pledged to deliver 10 F-16s by the end of 2026, up from three previously planned, and discussed supplying additional ammunition, including 20-mm rounds produced by Belgian defense company FN Herstal.
Jet-powered drones pose a growing challenge
Russia’s faster attack drones are harder to intercept than older, propeller-driven Shahed-type models. Their speed gives air defenders less time to respond and makes them more difficult for many interceptor drones and conventional short-range weapons to catch.
Ukraine’s air-to-air missile shortages have also increased the importance of F-16 cannon ammunition. Ukrainian pilots have sometimes relied on their aircraft’s built-in 20-mm cannon when air-to-air missiles are scarce.
Ukraine’s F-16s are so short of Western missiles that pilots fall back on jet’s built-in M61A1 Vulcan cannon, which risks killing civilians below
The threat from jet-powered drones is growing. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in late September that Ukraine was intercepting about 55% of Russia’s jet-powered drones, compared with more than 90% of older models.
Denmark’s ammunition delivery gives Ukrainian F-16 pilots more rounds to engage these faster targets, as Ukraine works to strengthen its defenses against Russia’s expanding drone campaign.

Competition in the tourism category of Latvia’s Export and Innovation Awards 2026 has reached a record high, with 36 applications submitted – more than ever before. Twelve applicants have advanced to the second round, while the jury has already heard presentations from 11 companies in the New Exporter category. Meanwhile, on-site evaluations of Latvia’s leading exporters and innovators are underway. The winners of Latvia’s highest national business awards will be announced on 3 December.
As part of the selection process, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) has reviewed the performance of more than 100 Latvian companies. Applicants in all five categories are evaluated in two rounds. Companies could apply directly in two categories, while candidates in the remaining three categories were nominated based on data from the Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia. The winner of each category will be announced at the awards ceremony on 3 December.
The Export and Innovation Awards are Latvia’s highest national recognition for business excellence and are being held for the 21st time this year. The competition honours companies whose achievements in exports, innovation and the creation of high added value strengthen Latvia’s economy. The jury assesses not only companies’ past performance but also their development strategies, investments and ability to compete in international markets. The competition is held under the patronage of the President of Latvia, Edgars Rinkēvičs.
“The record level of interest in the tourism category demonstrates that Latvian businesses are increasingly developing their offerings for international visitors and seeking opportunities to compete in global markets. The presentations by new exporters also reveal companies with serious ambitions and a clear understanding of their growth paths.
“A company’s potential cannot be assessed solely on the basis of turnover or export growth. It is equally important to consider the knowledge and technologies it applies, its investments in development and the strength of its vision for the future. On-site evaluations allow the jury to see far more than financial indicators alone.
“For companies that have already advanced to the second round, this represents significant national recognition of their achievements and an opportunity to showcase their work to a professional jury. The value of these awards lies in rigorous competition and professional assessment. Our aim is to ensure that receiving an award serves as a credible mark of Latvian business excellence internationally,” emphasises Ieva Jāgere, Director of the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA).
New Exporters Demonstrate Strong Growth Ambitions
The New Exporter category, organised by LIAA in cooperation with the Latvian Exporters Association “The Red Jackets”, received 14 applications this year. Twelve companies advanced to the second round.
On 13 and 14 October, the jury heard presentations from 11 companies, reviewing their achievements in international markets, export strategies and future development plans.
A key element of the evaluation is the companies’ ability not only to enter new markets but also to generate high added value in Latvia. The jury examined investments in product and service quality, production development, sustainability and the strengthening of competitiveness.
The category was open to companies with export turnover ranging from EUR 50,000 to EUR 1 million in 2025 and ambitions to reach EUR 5 million in export turnover within five years. The winner will receive a EUR 10,000 cash prize.
“Every successful exporter was once a newcomer. This category helps identify companies that, through ambition, expertise and consistent effort, have the potential to become the future of Latvian exports. In my opinion, this is the most interesting category in the competition, as it brings together a wide variety of companies, diverse products and remarkable entrepreneurs,” says Kaspars Rožkalns, Chairman of the Council of the Latvian Exporters Association “The Red Jackets”.
Tourism Category Sets a New Application Record
Latvian tourism businesses and organisations have demonstrated unprecedented interest in the Most Export-Capable New Tourism Product category.
A total of 36 applications were submitted, with 12 tourism products selected for the second round, which includes on-site evaluations.
The competition assesses tourism products introduced to the market within the past two years that can attract international visitors, offer high-quality and distinctive experiences, and generate high added value.
The jury pays particular attention to the products’ competitiveness in international markets, innovation, sustainability and potential to contribute to the development of Latvia’s tourism industry.
Applicants compete in two groups: small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and a separate group comprising associations, foundations, planning regions and municipalities.
The winner in the SME group will receive a EUR 10,000 cash prize.
Jury Conducts On-Site Evaluations of Latvia’s Export and Innovation Leaders
The second round has also begun in the Export Champion, Export Growth Leader and Innovation Champion categories.
Candidates in these categories were selected using data compiled by the Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia on company performance.
Advancing to the second round represents significant recognition of a company’s achievements. Candidates have been selected based on their performance at the national level and remain in contention for Latvia’s highest business award.
The jury’s visits provide an opportunity to gain first-hand insight into the companies whose achievements have placed them among the contenders for this prestigious recognition.
During these visits, jury members examine business operations, development strategies, investments in new products and technologies, and opportunities for growth in international markets.
The on-site meetings complement the analysis of statistical data and enable the jury to assess companies’ long-term competitive advantages.
For participating businesses, the visits also provide an opportunity to present their achievements directly to the jury, explain their development plans and demonstrate the strengths underpinning their competitiveness.
The Export Champion category recognises companies with outstanding export achievements. The Export Growth Leader category honours rapid expansion in international markets, while the Innovation Champion category highlights investments in research, development and the implementation of innovations.
The competition jury brings together experts in business, exports, innovation and tourism. The names of the shortlisted companies will not be disclosed until the competition results are announced.
Winners to Be Honoured in December
The Export and Innovation Awards 2026 are organised by the Ministry of Economics of Latvia and the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA), in cooperation with the Latvian Exporters Association “The Red Jackets”, the Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia and the state-owned development finance institution ALTUM.
The winners will be announced at a formal awards ceremony on 3 December.
Award recipients will receive a specially designed statuette created by artists, a diploma from the Ministry of Economics and the right to use the competition’s official award mark in their product communications and marketing materials.
In addition, EUR 10,000 cash prizes will be awarded to the winner of the New Exporter category and the winner of the SME group in the tourism category.
Further information about the competition is available on the LIAA website.
